articles.title: Avião da Gol faz pouso de emergência após decolar de Goiânia | G1
articles.standfirst: A aeronave transportava 180 pessoas, sendo 174 passageiros e seis tripulantes, quando precisou retornar ao Aeroporto de Goiânia após uma forte pancada durante a decolagem.
articles.summary: Avião da Gol com 190 pessoas a bordo declarou emergência e retornou ao Aeroporto de Goiânia após decolar com destino a Congonhas.
articles.body:
Um avião com 180 pessoas precisou retornar ao Aeroporto de Goiânia e fazer um pouso de emergência na manhã deste sábado (12), poucos minutos após a decolagem. Segundo o Aeroporto Internacional de Goiânia, a aeronave da Gol, com 174 passageiros e seis tripulantes, partiu de Goiânia com destino ao Aeroporto de Congonhas, em São Paulo, mas declarou emergência e retornou ao aeroporto de Goiânia, onde recebeu apoio durante o pouso.

De acordo com o aeroporto, a aeronave pousou normalmente, sem intercorrências (leia nota completa abaixo). A administração informou ainda que a companhia aérea presta suporte aos passageiros.

Em nota, a Gol Linhas Aéreas informou que o voo foi cancelado após apresentar problemas técnicos. A companhia afirmou que todas as medidas operacionais foram adotadas com foco na segurança e que os passageiros impactados recebem o suporte previsto nas normas da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac).

Avião faz pouso forçado em Gioânia logo após decolar — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhaguera

Segundo apuração da TV Anhanguera, a aeronave ficou cerca de 45 minutos no ar antes de retornar ao Aeroporto de Goiânia. Um passageiro contou à reportagem que a decolagem estava prevista para 9h05, mas o avião saiu com atraso, às 9h50. Logo após o início da decolagem, os passageiros sentiram uma forte pancada na aeronave. Pouco depois, foram informados de que o avião precisaria retornar ao aeroporto.

Imagens do site FlightRadar mostram que a aeronave deu ao menos dez voltas após a decolagem, antes de retornar para Goiânia (veja o vídeo acima).

Passageiros relatam momentos de tensão durante o voo

Em entrevista à TV, o passageiro Rafael Grabowski relatou momentos de pânico cerca de 20 minutos após a decolagem. Segundo ele, houve um estrondo na lateral esquerda da aeronave e diversos objetos caíram. Rafael contou que a maior angústia foi a falta de avisos da tripulação enquanto o avião dava voltas para queimar combustível antes do pouso de emergência.

"O pouso foi tranquilo, mas a aeronave ficou sobrevoando a região por bastante tempo sem esclarecimentos. Somente depois fomos avisados sobre a necessidade do pouso. Todo o procedimento demorou e a espera foi muito estressante", disse à TV.

"O Aeroporto de Goiânia informa que uma aeronave da GOL que decolou com destino a São Paulo (Congonhas) retornou ao terminal após declaração de emergência pela tripulação. O pouso ocorreu normalmente e em total segurança, sem registro de intercorrências. A operação recebeu o apoio previsto nos protocolos aeroportuários, e a companhia aérea está prestando assistência aos passageiros."

articles.title: Las Palmas encuentra el rumbo ante un Cádiz a la deriva que aún no ganó
articles.standfirst: El cuadro canario fue infinitamente superior a los amarillos y se llevaron el triunfo con un gol de Enrique Clemente
articles.summary: El cuadro canario fue infinitamente superior a los amarillos y se llevaron el triunfo con un gol de Enrique Clemente
articles.body: Las Palmas se impuso por 0-1 al Cádiz gracias a un gol de Enrique Clemente en la segunda mitad que sigue agravando la crisis deportiva que vive el cuadro cadista. El conjunto canario fue superior durante buena parte del encuentro y supo gestionar su ventaja ante un equipo local que intentó reaccionar, pero que apenas generó peligro y que suma un pobre bagaje de tres puntos de quince posibles en el inicio liguero. El fuerte viento condicionó un partido cuya primera ocasión correspondió a Borja Vázquez, que cabeceó por encima del larguero un centro de Álvaro García Pascual en el minuto 2. Las Palmas tomó progresivamente el control y Bonfanti llegó a marcar en el 24, aunque el VAR anuló el tanto por una mano previa de Miyashiro. El Cádiz también vio invalidado un gol de Álvaro García Pascual por fuera de juego de Borja Vázquez. Antes del descanso, Jesé obligó a intervenir a Ezkieta, mientras que Iván Jaime estrelló un balón en el palo nada más comenzar la segunda parte. La absoluta superioridad visitante encontró premio en el minuto 60. Miyashiro disparó desde la frontal, Ezkieta rechazó el balón y Enrique Clemente aprovechó la segunda jugada para firmar el único gol del encuentro. Dos minutos después, Álvaro García Pascual pudo empatar tras un error de Caro, pero el guardameta corrigió su fallo con una buena parada. El Cádiz buscó la igualada con la entrada de Efe y Vladys también estuvo cerca de aprovechar un error de Juanma Herzog, aunque Las Palmas defendió su ventaja sin excesivos apuros. El conjunto gaditano prolonga su mal comienzo y sigue sin ganar: suma tres puntos de quince posibles. Las Palmas, pese a que Rubén de la Barrera admitió en la previa que su equipo tenía más puntos que sensaciones, continúa sumando, vuelve a ganar y se mantiene en la zona alta de Segunda División.

articles.title: Holt firma el mejor arranque histórico del Madrid CFF
articles.standfirst: Un gol de pizarra de la danesa sella la victoria ante el Sevilla y mantiene el pleno de victorias del conjunto capitalino
articles.summary: Un gol de pizarra de la danesa sella la victoria ante el Sevilla y mantiene el pleno de victorias del conjunto capitalino
articles.body: El Madrid CFF se impuso al Sevilla (1-0) en el Fernando Torres de Fuenlabrada, firmando así el pleno de victorias en lo que llevamos de curso, siendo además su mejor arranque en su andadura en la máxima categoría del mal llamado fútbol femenino nacional. Las locales se adelantaron el marcador justo cuando se cumplía el séptimo minuto de juego en una jugada de pizarra. Un córner sacado por Ana, haciendo la pared con Diki en el primer palo y Holt, llegando desde atrás, empalando la pelota en el punto de penalti mandando el balón a la jaula sin que Sullastres pudiera hacer nada. El Sevilla intentó reaccionar y llegó a empatar, pero sin que el gol llegara a subir al marcador. Fue una falta botada por Gemma en la que Ulloa falla en la salida y Marques cabecea al fondo de la red, pero la colegiada entendió fue había habido falta a la guardameta. Las visitantes intentaron sin suerte equilibrar el marcador en el segundo acto. Más cerca estuvo el Madrid CFF, que llegó a marcar a diez minutos para el final -un cabezazo de León tras saque de esquina botado por Ana-, pero se anuló tras consulta con el FVS al entender que había existido falta en el salto. En el tiempo de añadido, Ulloa voló para sacar un remate de Castelló que sonaba a empate. Granada (3-1), Valencia (1-3) y Sevilla (1-0) han sido las tres víctimas del Madrid CFF en el arranque liguero. Nunca antes, desde su aparición en la élite (temporada 2017/18), había llegado a la cuarta jornada con nueve puntos en su haber. El próximo sábado tendrá la opción de seguir la racha midiéndose al Espanyol en la Ciudad Deportiva Dani Jarque.

articles.title: Bournemouth 2-2 Brentford: Kevin Schade scores twice as Marco Rose remains in wait of first Premier League win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Kevin Schade nets twice to keep Bournemouth winless in the Premier League; Brentford took the lead though Schade before Patrick Kluivert equalised; Marcus Tavernier then put Bournemouth ahead before Dorde Petrovic's header ensured a Schade second
articles.body:
Schade headed Brentford in front in the first half before Justin Kluivert levelled four minutes before the break. Marcus Tavernier, who scored his third of the season, then put Bournemouth ahead eight minutes after half-time, leaving Rose dreaming of a first Premier League victory.

Latest news and rumours: Bournemouth | Brentford

However, Dorde Petrovic's lax ball out from the back was seized upon just three minutes later by Schade, who struck again to restore parity.

Bournemouth have now led in all four of their Premier League games this season without winning any of them. They had already become only the second side to do so in their opening three matches, after Chelsea in 1992/93.

It continues a worrying trend for Bourneouth, who have dropped more points from winning positions than any other Premier League team since the start of last season. They had also surrendered a two-goal lead against Newcastle last weekend.

Brentford, meanwhile, remain unbeaten in their opening four league games under Keith Andrews, although they have now dropped points from winning positions in three successive matches themselves.

The Bees also extend their unbeaten league run against Bournemouth to 12 games, having not lost this fixture since August 2014.

For Bournemouth, there were further signs of progress but another missed opportunity. For Brentford, it was another recovery that keeps their unbeaten start intact.

The key moments from the Vitality Stadium

7: WIDE! Tavernier puts it on a dime with a brilliant set-piece delivery from the left. Silva meets it but completely misses the target. He should have scored!

34: GOAL! Yarmoliuk digs out a cross after Bournemouth failed to clear their lines. Schade meets it heading towards goal, Petrovic gets a hand to it but he's still beaten.

37: RAYAN SHOULD EQUALISE! Rayan blazes a rebound over the bar after a beautiful Bournemouth move forward.

38: GOAL! Bournemouth keep up the pressure. Rayan pokes the ball into Evanilson who bundles his way into the box. It falls to Kluivert who improvises well, stretching to fire at goal.

45+6: BRENTFORD WANT A PENALTY! They feel Adrien Truffert has handled the ball as he attempted to block it.

HALF TIME! The whistle blows as VAR checks the handball. It's not given and the players retreat into the tunnel.

53: GOAL! Tavernier scores again as Bournemouth turn it around at the Vitality, drilling home to make it 2-1.

56: GOAL! Petrovic produces howler, giving the ball to Schade to score a second.

"I think we do enough to win games. It's just about the momentum, the situation. But I'm quite sure that we're going to change it if we just continue with our hard work.

"I feel like we should have won the game, but it hasn't happened, so it's a draw. I'm very pleased with the performance. I love our attitude and how convinced we are about the way we want to play. In both boxes would be nice [to be more efficient], because if you concede two goals, you need to score three.

"Brentford is a tough opponent, so we avoided many situations right after they started to get difficult to handle."

Andrews: We didn't deserve to win but we showed resilience

"We didn't deserve the three points, would be my assessment. We didn't play as efficiently and effectively enough as we would have liked today. We lacked a little bit of cohesion at times.

"I think it was more on us. We didn't do certain things well. But I have to say the grit and character and resilience that we showed to get a point away from home, still be unbeaten, is obviously a positive."

On Kevin Schade: "He's been excellent, the way he's attacked everything we've done, regardless of where he plays, what he gets asked to do with the ball, without the ball, there's such an honesty to his game.

"I felt like it's been bubbling with him. The goals, you can see the goal he scored against Leeds, the confidence he's playing with, and today [Saturday] the way he took those two goals again was really nice."

Analysis: Are Rose's Bournemouth unlucky or do they have a deep issue?

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

"Bournemouth are now the first team to lead in each of their opening four Premier League games of a season and fail to win any of them.

"Marco Rose said was clear after their Newcastle draw that game management was something they needed to remedy. You can't help but feel a touch sympathetic for a side freely creating as they are.

"They took 20 shots with 10 being on target, while Brentford only tested Dorde Petrovic's goal twice. You'd expect to win the game off those statistics alone.

"The concern will be the speed at which they allowed Brentford back in, though.

"Today, they went 2-1 up and conceded again within three minutes. Brentford didn't have to wait long to find a way back into the game, and that's becoming the recurring theme for Bournemouth.

"There's clearly enough in this team to win football matches. But until they can control those periods after scoring, and prevent opponents from immediately regaining momentum, they're going to keep leaving points on the table.

"Four games, four leads, no wins. Welcome to the Premier League, Marco Rose."

articles.title: Barnet 2-1 Accrington
articles.summary: Charlie Lakin’s second-half brace ensured Barnet got back to winning ways by beating Accrington 2-1 at the Hive.
articles.body:
The first real chance fell to the visitors in the 13th minute when captain Shaun Whalley's low drive towards the far post forced Barnet goalkeeper Matthew Cox into a fine save, before Devon Matthews headed wide from the resulting corner.

The Reds took the lead in the 27th minute, with Charlie Caton lobbing the ball over Cox and into the net.

The hosts almost responded immediately after Oisin Gallagher's ambitious effort was brilliantly saved by Accrington goalkeeper Louie Moulden, with Danny Collinge heading wide moments later.

Barnet levelled before the hour mark when Damola Ajayi found Adam Senior, who cut inside and squared for Lakin to fire home.

Lakin claimed his second when he pounced on some hesitancy to fire past Moulden and put the hosts ahead.

Two minutes later, Accrington were reduced to 10 men when Matthews received a second yellow card for a two-footed challenge on Lakin. The Bees held on to secure victory.

articles.title: Manolo González: “Hemos de ser un equipo lo más ambicioso posible”
articles.standfirst: El técnico perico se mostraba satisfecho con el partido y el trabajo de los suyos
articles.summary: El técnico perico se mostraba satisfecho con el partido y el trabajo de los suyos
articles.body: El Espanyol se ha impuesto ante Osasuna en Pamplona. Los de Manolo González superaban a los rojillos gracias a dos tantos de Roberto Fernández en los primeros compases de partido. El equipo perico encarrilaba rápido un encuentro que ha dominado y controlado desde el inicio. La victoria sabe a oro para un Espanyol que suma el primer triunfo del curso como visitante. Manolo González se mostraba satisfecho en rueda de prensa tras el partido por el resultado y el partido que han jugado los suyos. El técnico ensalzaba el nivel que ha mostrado el Espanyol, tanto en ataque como en defensa y explicaba que las acciones de los goles son fruto del trabajo de la semana. Un buen partido del equipo: “Ha sido un buen partido. Al final no sé si redondo o no, porque como siempre tenemos tendencia a sacar lo malo. No sé si ha sido un partido redondo, pero ha sido un partido completo, en un campo complicado, con un rival que te exige a nivel de centros, de presencia en área. Creo que hemos estado bien, que hemos tenido momentos buenos de juego, además. Y bueno, queda mucho por hacer, mucho trabajo por crecer, estamos en la jornada 5 y nos queda mucho camino y mucho trabajo todavía”. El trabajo de la semana da frutos: “Queda de iluminado decirlo, los goles sí que son situaciones que se habían trabajado en un lado, que se han dado en el lado derecho nuestro, no en izquierdo. El izquierdo se habían trabajado con un perfil que era Hinojo, que abandonase la posición de salida de tres para incorporarse en el lado derecho, era con Marcos y con Edu y liberando a Clemens. De hecho uno de los goles ha sido así, ha sido un balón a Edu, que se ha liberado y ha metido el pase al espacio a Omar. Por suerte ha salido bien y lo que buscamos es esto, que el equipo mejore día a día en situaciones de atacar el área, situaciones de encontrar a espalda rival, que pienso que es lo que te da mucha ventaja”. Gran nivel defensivo del equipo: “Ellos han tenido la del saque de banda, que es una que hemos preparado nosotros muy bien. Lo que te decía antes, hemos cometido dos errores muy graves, el gol anulado y la situación del saque de banda, que es un pase atrás que han rematado dentro del área a las manos de Marco. Y son dos situaciones que es mérito de ellos las dos, sobre todo la segunda, por sacar rápido, pero es un momento que nos vamos del partido. Esto es lo que estamos hablando y que como equipo para mí tenemos que corregir urgente, porque a veces nos pasa. Pero sí que es verdad que hemos defendido bien el área, el equipo ha estado muy bien, Lele ha estado sensacional y Hinojo que, con la edad que tiene, ha estado muy bien. Estoy muy contento con el equipo, Urko ha hecho un gran partido, muy contento con el equipo, cuando ha tocado jugar hemos podido jugar y cuando ha tocado remangarse nos ha tocado remangarnos y lo hemos hecho bien. Así que contento porque ganar aquí nunca es fácil”. El equipo ha atacado bien: “En las acciones de gol hemos juntado pases en la zona, Marcos ha encontrado la ventaja muy bien en el primer gol y claro, eso te da la vida, porque eliminas a cinco jugadores de golpe del rival. Creo que hemos conseguido sumar tres pases, antes de dar un pase arriesgado, pero era claro. Eso te hace que elimines jugadores del rival y te hace que puedas atacar a la línea mucho mejor, que es lo que ha pasado. Pienso que también ha sido un gran mérito de los jugadores encontrar estas situaciones, porque lo han hecho fenomenal”. Importante ganar a domicilio: “Es que es vital. Es vital porque es lo que te digo, vas a ir a campo del Rayo, te van a apretar, vas a ir al campo que toque de la Liga y te van a apretar. Ya vemos que ganar fuera de casa en Primera División cuesta mucho a todo el mundo, no a nosotros. El Alavés venía con una racha muy buena y no ha podido ganar en campo del Racing y está haciendo las cosas fenomenal. Los partidos fuera son difíciles. Nos tenemos que adaptar a esto, hacernos muy fuertes en casa y fuera, pues ser un equipo lo más ambicioso posible. Después veremos el tope dónde está, pero repito, nos queda mucho camino, mucho, igual que el domingo con el Sevilla nos queda mucho camino y no nos podemos parar, tenemos que seguir avanzando”.

articles.title: Texas fan who drilled $1.2M College GameDay kick leaves Matthew McConaughey hanging
articles.summary: What an eventful morning on College GameDay.
articles.body:
A Texas Longhorns fan named Connor woke up today with great excitement for his team's primetime matchup against Ohio State—an early test of top-five teams that could go a long way in shaping the College Football Playoff picture. Perhaps he already knew that he would be participating in Pat McAfee's College GameDay kicking contest or maybe that's something that materialized on site. However that went down, he is having an absolutely unforgettable day as he became college football's main character by successfully converting the kick and sending the Austin crowd into delirium.

It was an awesome moment and made even better when our newfound protagonist made it clear that he intended to donate half of the $1.2 million prize to charity.

This right here is what it's all about. Connor is pitching about as perfect a game as a non-athlete can pitch on the sporting stage. Except for one thing.

He left Matthew McConaughey hanging amid all the chaos after this life-changing boot. Totally understandable given the moment. And something that the official College GameDay account had fun with after the fact.

MORE: Best 'College GameDay' signs from Week 2: Ohio State vs Texas

Considering the classy move and everything going on, surely this is alright, alright, alright with the actor. And it better be. Connor must be protected at all costs.

Texas has a chance to make an already great day jump up into the stratosphere if they can knock off the Buckeyes later on tonight in the massive matchup. Everything seems to be coming up Connor so don't bet against them.

articles.body:
Atlético 's U-20 team wrapped up its final training session in preparation for the derby against América, valid for the 8th round of the Campeonato Mineiro Decagonal. The match will take place this Sunday (13) at 10 a.m. at CT Lanna Drumond, with live coverage on the Bola e Batom Channel on YouTube. Click here to watch.

The team coached by Henrique Teixeira leads the Decagonal with 13 points. Despite being tied on points with the runner-up and third-place team, Atlético remains on top thanks to its number of wins (4) and goals scored (15).

In the last round, the Crias beat Betim 4-0 and took over first place. The goals were scored by forwards Murillo, Mosquito (2), and Riquelme.

The match against América will be Atlético's penultimate one in the Decagonal. Atlético will close out its campaign on September 19 against Nacional de Muriaé at 3 p.m. at Cidade do Galo.

In midweek, Galo made its debut in the U-20 Copa do Brasil with a 4-0 thrashing of Sobradinho, from the Federal District, at Arena MRV.

articles.title: Crystal Palace 2-3 Ipswich: What O'Neil and Flemming said
articles.summary: It is tough to win away from home in the Premier League is a newly-promoted side.  Ipswich Town's Emersonn is the first Brazilian player to both score and as...
articles.body:
Ipswich Town manager Gary O'Neil, speaking to Sky Sports: "I'm pleased for the players and the fanbase. It is tough to win away from home in the Premier League is a newly-promoted side. We've done it after the second away game of the season.

"Fantastic character, three good goals and we look like a threat. Plenty of positives. There is lots we need to improve but in terms of character, there was some big pluses."

Ipswich Town forward Zian Flemming speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "It's a great feeling to win, and to score the winner is even better. They had a phase in the second half - regardless of being down to 10 men - where they were the dominant side, and they rewarded themselves with a goal as well. Luckily we turned it around as we shouldn't really be in that situation in the first place."

On his low-key celebration: "I can't really predict how I'm going to celebrate. I felt quite calm in the moment for some reason."

On the win: "Every point is precious. It is not easy to win in the Premier League, especially away from home. We were playing against 10 man for a big part of the game so we should have come away with three points as well. They are all helping towards the end goal."

This is the first time that Ipswich Town have won a Premier League game in which they trailed since a 2-1 away win over Tottenham Hotspur in December 2001.

Ipswich Town's Emersonn is the first Brazilian player to both score and assist for a newly promoted side in the Premier League since Danilo for Nottingham Forest against Southampton in May 2023.

articles.title: Dan Campbell Tells Amon-Ra St. Brown Where Lions Would Take Him in 2021 Redraft
articles.summary: Dan Campbell revealed that Brad Holmes was targeting Amon-Ra St. Brown well before Detroit selected him 112th overall in 2021.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions selected Penei Sewell seventh overall in the 2021 NFL Draft.

If Dan Campbell could do that draft again knowing what he knows now, Detroit apparently would not wait very long before making its second pick.

During his appearance on the St. Brown Podcast , Campbell revealed just how highly he and general manager Brad Holmes viewed Amon-Ra St. Brown before Detroit eventually selected him 112th overall.

"Brad had already been full tilt into it. He was already talking about this receiver from USC that he'd been watching for two years, three years, whatever it was. He was already on you before I was."

That part matters. St. Brown did not become a classic fourth-round lottery ticket that Detroit stumbled into. Holmes had been studying him long before draft weekend.

What happened next was a calculated gamble on value.

Campbell Saw the Same Player Detroit Has Today

Campbell eventually dug into the film himself, and the characteristics that jumped out sound awfully familiar five years later.

"I just remember you were a freaking pit bull, man. You were at the college level what you are here. You get after dudes. You were the most physical receiver coming out that year."

Campbell was not merely talking about St. Brown throwing blocks.

"I'm not just talking about blocking. The blocking was big, but I'm talking about the way you separated at the top of routes, the way you broke out, your play speed. Your college play speed — the speed didn't matter. Your play speed was fast, and you were a football player. That was evident."

Detroit's original 2021 draft profile of St. Brown praised his route running, body control and ability to win contested catches. The Lions also knew the measurable that would make some teams hesitate. St. Brown ran a 4.51-second 40-yard dash at his pro day.

Campbell clearly did not care much about the stopwatch.

The Lions Loved St. Brown but Played the Draft

This is where Campbell's explanation gets particularly interesting from a draft-strategy perspective.

Detroit liked the player. Holmes apparently liked him very early. Yet the Lions still waited until the fourth round.

"Brad and I were on you. He was on you first, but I loved you, man. We were on your ass. It was just about, when do we acquire you? When do we get the most value, bang for buck, and make sure we've got a chance to get you?"

Campbell followed with the sentence that essentially explains every draft room in America.

"You don't know how everything's going to turn out, but you know a football player when you see one."

The Lions eventually selected St. Brown at No. 112 , after 16 wide receivers had already come off the board. Detroit believed it had identified something other teams were undervaluing, then kept waiting because it believed St. Brown would remain available.

It also could have gone spectacularly wrong.

Then Amon-Ra asked the question that really mattered.

Knowing everything Detroit knows now, how long would Campbell have waited in a 2021 redraft?

"Had we truly known then what we know now, we'd have traded up right behind Penei and drafted your ass."

Campbell did not specify an exact selection, so there is no reason to pretend he literally announced St. Brown as the No. 8 pick in a hypothetical redraft. The meaning is still unmistakable: Detroit would take Sewell, then immediately begin trying to get St. Brown.

And hindsight has made the case easy. St. Brown has developed into one of Detroit's defining players and is now a four-time team captain. When the Lions announced their seven captains for 2026 , St. Brown already ranked first in franchise history through a player's first five Lions seasons in receptions, receiving yards and 100-yard games.

Brad Holmes' Evaluation Looks Better With Time

The fun part of Campbell's story is the imaginary redraft.

The more important part is what it says about Holmes.

St. Brown's production makes it easy now to say everybody should have drafted him higher. That is hindsight doing what hindsight does. Holmes was apparently pounding the table before any of those NFL receptions existed.

Detroit then had to answer a much more difficult question: How long can we wait without losing him?

St. Brown's physicality remains one of the traits that separates him, and new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing recently said the receiver's leadership, intensity and physicality had "blown me away" .

Five years later, Campbell is still describing essentially the same player he saw on USC film.

Detroit just did not fully understand how good that player was going to become.

They'll be particularly motivated to get things moving in the right direction.

I suspect the Black Cats will be a stern test for the Gunners. But Arsenal are no slouches, either. They've been playing really, really well lately. If they keep up their recent form, someone is going to be on the wrong end of a gaudy scoreline. Maybe it'll be today!

articles.title: Emery left searching for answers after another Villa loss
articles.summary: Aston Villa have lost three of their opening four Premier League games to leave boss Unai Emery struggling for answers.
articles.body:
Defender Tyrone Mings summed up the Aston Villa mood as he slumped to the floor at full-time following a 2-1 defeat at home to Nottingham Forest .

Three defeats in their opening four games only leaves further questions for manager Unai Emery to answer following a summer rebuild.

Villa may have ended a run of 372 Premier League minutes without a Premier League goal but their problems remain.

If Coventry beat Brighton on Sunday, Emery's side will sit bottom of the table.

It is the fourth time they have started a top-flight season without winning any of their opening four games, having done so in 1992-93, 1997-98 and 2025-26.

It mirrors last season - which ended with a fourth-placed Premier League finish and historic Europe League triumph - but those celebrations from May already feel like a lifetime ago.

Emery questions why McAtee was not sent off

A late Igor Jesus winner meant Oliver Glasner is now unbeaten in his eight games against Emery and, after a first win as Forest boss, he will view this as one of the sweetest.

Liam Delap scored just 45 seconds after the restart and, while Alysson levelled for Villa with his first goal in English football, the visitors were deserved winners.

Jesus pounced ahead of Aaron Wan-Bissaka with two minutes left to earn a first win at Villa Park since 1994 as Forest took advantage of Villa's misfortune.

By then they were down to 10 men after full-back Ian Maatsen was forced off injured, with Emery using all his substitutes to add to their defensive problems.

There is a fear the left-back's ankle injury could keep him out for a considerable time, meaning new signing Matteo Ruggeri will be called on, perhaps earlier than Emery would want.

The Villa boss complained Forest attacker James McAtee should have been sent off for the challenge which injured Maatsen, but refused to blame it for the outcome of the match.

"When we equalised the match could change but we finished with Ian Maatsen injured and with 10 players, we conceded so many chances in the last minutes and they scored the second goal and deserved it," he said.

"But after watching it on TV, I think the VAR should call the referee because it's a clear tackle behind the player and, for me, it should be a red card.

"Of course, they deserved it (the win), but the decision of the referee should be different. We finished the match in Brighton, two yellow cards for Joao Gomes , and we accepted it. But today, after the injury of Maatsen, and we're finishing with 10.

"He didn't want to injure our player but if we can watch it through the TV, it's a VAR action, and to call the referee and should be a red card, and maybe finishing with 10 v 10 was maybe different in the match.

"But it's not an excuse how we play the second half. We played so so poor, and this is our work and our responsibility or my responsibility."

Centre-back Pau Torres was also replaced in the first half to leave Villa's backline increasingly thin, with summer signing Taylor Harwood-Bellis omitted from the squad again.

Villa visit Coventry in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday before a trip to Tottenham and the £30m centre-back will be expecting a chance at the CBS Arena.

They were unable to cope with a rejuvenated Delap - who also had a goal disallowed - and the visitors had 22 shots.

Glasner's men also had 32 touches in Villa's box as an ineffective home attack struggled again.

Bar a comical scramble, where Victor Lindelof failed to net after a combination of Matz Sels , Murillo and the post denied him, they created little.

Nicolas Jackson was replaced at half-time with his replacement Tammy Abraham - a player Emery wanted to sell this summer - because Emery feared the Senegal striker would get sent off after an early yellow card.

Brazilian Alysson was also introduced and glanced in John McGinn 's cross against the run of play, before Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye - the pair costing a combined £98m - made their debuts as second-half substitutes, but were unable to make a difference.

Alejandro Garnacho was again an unused substitute, with the Chelsea loanee so far failing to impress Emery to get game time.

A first win at Villa Park since 1994 was deserved for Forest as the hosts' home record continued to crumble.

They had not lost at home in the league for 12 months before Glasner's former club Crystal Palace won 3-0 last August.

Since then - with Glasner also winning 2-1 with the Eagles in the Carabao Cup - Villa Park has become less of a fortress.

They lost four of their final 15 home league games last season, while also relying on late goals to rescue a point against Leeds and beat Brighton and Sunderland .

A 3-1 FA Cup exit to Newcastle also exposed the frailties at Villa Park, which have continued this season with an opening 1-0 defeat at home to champions Arsenal followed by the loss to Forest.

Along with a new squad after several key departures, the North Stand redevelopment has meant the capacity has been reduced and there are no fans at one end.

But the drop off at home should now be alarming.

Villa won at home when it mattered most at the end of last season - routing Forest in the Europa League semi-final en route to winning the competition and putting four past Liverpool to book a Champions League spot - but they need to rediscover the feeling which made them near-invincible in front of their own followers.

So often over the past few seasons, after a Villa equaliser, they have they gone on to win, but there was no grandstand finish this time, leaving Emery perplexed about why his side could not control the game.

"I don't know why," he said. "I want to see the match again and to understand why we lost our shape."

Jesus instead had the final say to leave the Spaniard, who has provided solutions at Villa for so long during his tenure, searching for answers to revive his side's fortunes.

articles.body: El Girona perdió 1-2 ante un Castellón, que no tuvo respuesta a un gran inicio local, con gol de Junior en el minuto 7, pero que si encontró soluciones a lo largo del encuentro para pasara a dominar, implantar su juego, su ritmo y, ya en la segunda parte, con uno más por la expulsión inocente de Abel Ruiz, remontar el encuentro gracias a los tantos de Sienra (81’) y Álvaro (86’) a rechace después de dos paradones de Gazzaniga. La puesta en escena local, por intensidad en la presión, la circulación de balón y la verticalidad, fue mucho mejor que la de un Castellón errático y sin capacidad para implantar su ritmo y juego. Temprano, los de Quique Álvarez se avanzaron con un tanto del joven Junior, que aprovechó un rechace de Matthys en el intento de parar un disparo de Fran Beltrán desde la frontal (7’). Antes de la media hora la tendencia cambió gracias a un Castellón que empezó a superar líneas de presión de los locales. Y gracias a esto Barri tuvo una gran ocasión para empatar con un remate de cabeza que obligó a Gazzaniga a estirarse para enviar a córner con la punta de los dedos (43’). Vanat, antes del descanso, también pudo hacer el 2-0, pero tiró al muñeco en el uno contra uno ante el portero (45’). La segunda parte fue un monólogo del Castellón al que le anularon un gol en el 47' obra de Juanjo Nieto. El asedio blanquinegro aumentó con la expulsión de Abel Ruiz en el 52' y, después de estar cerca del gol con remates de Camara y Barri, en el 81', un centro de Suero acabó con un primer cabezazo de Camara con paradón de Gazzaniga, pero con Sienra atento al rechace para hacer la igualada. Tan solo cinco minutos después, Camara recibió al espacio y se sacó un buen disparo cruzado que de nuevo Gazzaniga repelió, pero Álvaro García, muy atento, metió al fondo de la portería (86’). Premio justo para el Castellón, duro golpe para el Girona.

articles.title: Premier League: Which goalkeepers have the most clean sheets?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team look at which goalkeepers have achieved 100 Premier League clean sheets.
articles.body:
Jordan Pickford has become only the 19th goalkeeper to keep 100 or more clean sheets in the Premier League.

He joined the club as Everton earned a 0-0 draw at Tottenham on Saturday.

Only one goalkeeper has achieved more than 200 clean sheets in the Premier League.

Petr Cech, with 202, is the leader in the league's shut-outs by a considerable margin, recording 33 more than his closest rival David James.

The former Czech Republic international also holds the Premier League record for the highest percentage of clean sheets per games played, and most consecutive clean sheets.

The former Chelsea and Arsenal stopper was also the fastest to 100 clean sheets.

Liverpool 's Alisson was the last goalkeeper prior to Pickford to join the 100 club, securing his century of top-flight clean sheets during a 0-0 draw with Leeds on 1 January 2026.

Newcastle 's Nick Pope is the next Premier League player in line to reach 100, sitting on 80 clean sheets, but is yet to feature this season after losing his number one spot in the team to Lukas Hornicek.

Former West Ham keeper Lukasz Fabianski came close to hitting the hundred mark, but spent the 2025-26 season sidelined with injury before retiring having reached 92 clean sheets.

Goalkeepers must play a full match to be credited with a clean sheet.

articles.title: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola bemoans lack of creativity and cutting edge against Fulham and explains Bradley Barcola plan
articles.summary: Liverpool were held to a goalless draw by Fulham as Andoni Iraola's wait for a first home Premier League win as Reds manager continues; Iraola: "I think it's the first game since I'm here, I think we've had problems to create chances, to score goals, to make the difference offensively."
articles.body:
The result leaves Iraola unbeaten so far this term, but Liverpool have yet to win at home in the Premier League this season.

Liverpool struggled to create opportunities against a Fulham team that had lost their opening three games, with Iraola insisting afterwards that his side's shortcomings were evident.

"I think what was lacking, I think it was quite clear," Iraola said.

"I think it's the first game since I'm here, I think we've had problems to create chances, to score goals, to make the difference offensively.

"That's the main reason. We couldn't create as many chances as we wanted and we haven't scored a goal. And that's why we go just with one point."

The Reds lacked the energy they showed in their midweek Champions League win over Atletico Madrid, but Iraola refused to use fatigue as an excuse for his side's failure to pick up all three points.

"I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it.

"I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60-something hours between the games, after a very big game (against Atletico Madrid) the other day.

"But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe. But sometimes it's going to happen the same way during the season. We have to adapt to these circumstances.

"It's this kind of game that you need to win, sometimes with a set play, sometimes with a shot from the edge, sometimes from a moment of brilliance from the offensive players and we haven't had that today.

"We've been clearly not as good offensively as we've been in other days."

Bradley Barcloa made his full Premier League debut in the game and was deployed from the left in a 4-2-3-1 formation, with Victor Munoz starting the game on the right.

Explaining his thinking, Iraola said: "I think I said it a lot of times. I think we have four wingers. Probably, before the season, everyone will say there are more left wingers than right wingers, because they play more there.

"I think all the wingers will play on the right and will play on the left. Depending on the match-up, depending on where we think they are going to be more dangerous, depending on the defensive demand, depending on what we feel, what we analyse, we position them in the right or in the left.

"But I think Bradley, I think everyone. The four of them already have played both sides and it's going to be a whole season like this because of the wingers, with a lot of times the same preferences."

Iraola added: "I think with Bradley now we are building also his physical condition, because he hasn't had any in pre-season and I think there is a good part where today he played, I think, a little bit more than three days ago against Atletico Madrid.

"He had a good chance in the second half, they blocked the shot but he arrived well.

"Probably, we know he has more, but now it's about giving him the minutes, keep building his confidence also and he's a player that is worthy of our support."

articles.title: Liverpool fail Fulham test as Chelsea's defensive problems continue to hamper their title challenge credentials - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: The Sky Sports football writers analyse Saturday's Premier League action as Liverpool fail to inspire in goalless draw with Fulham; Chelsea held by newly-promoted Hull in further showing of defensive frailties; Aston Villa have major attacking concerns
articles.body:
Much of the talk surrounding the Chelsea team that Xabi Alonso is in the midst of creating is what they are capable of in attack. How can you stop JP Morgan?

No one has been able to stop them from contributing at least one goal per game this season, but you can't bank on them to get you out of footballing bankruptcy if you can't keep clean sheets.

It is a problem that has impacted the Blues for some time, not just under Alonso. This is the 20th Premier League game in a row their defence has been breached.

The signing of a World Cup winner and multi-time Yashin trophy winner in the form of Emi Martinez is all well and good. However, if he has defenders not doing the basics in front of him, he may as well be Robert Sanchez.

The 1.32 xG that Hull managed was a fair reflection of how dangerous they were at times at Stamford Bridge. And it wasn't like they carved open the hosts. Most of the time, they had chances put on a plate.

The potential in attack is obvious, and certainly exciting. However, Alonso needs to tap into his learnings under Jose Mourinho and make this Chelsea side much tougher to score against if he wants to challenge. Callum Bishop

There were celebrations at Anfield on Wednesday when Andoni Iraola picked up the first Champions League win of his coaching career against Atletico Madrid. But that win was always going to come at some point this season. There was a bigger question.

One of the themes of this Liverpool season was always likely to be how the new coach would be able to cope with an increased schedule, having impressed at Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth without the added challenge of European commitments.

As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights

Latest news and rumours: Liverpool | Fulham

This was the first test of that and Liverpool did not pass it. They were unable to play at the tempo that Iraola usually demands, starting slowly and struggling to raise the level. Fulham were well worth their first point of the campaign and looked as likely to win it.

Iraola's unbeaten run as Liverpool boss continues, one that extends back to the first week of January for him personally given his exploits with the Cherries. But home games against Nottingham Forest and Fulham have yielded only two points. More is needed.

Asked in the press conference whether the fatigue explained Liverpool's performance, Iraola replied: "In the end, this is the easier one, for me, for you, for everyone - our players were tired. I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. We cannot hide it.

"I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60-something hours between the games, after a very big game the other day. But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe."

The onus is going to be on Iraola to find the answers. Adam Bate

It doesn't take a genius to figure out where Tottenham's biggest concern lies right now. You can't win games if you don't score goals. That's why Spurs haven't won a league game this season, after going 400 minutes without finding the net.

They have so many creative players, all of whom were on the pitch against the Toffees. Yet the man who they need to score the bulk of their goals was anonymous. Or at the very least, wasn't found.

Latest news and rumours: Tottenham | Everton

Dominic Solanke's fitness for Tottenham feels imperative. As the only out and out number nine available to De Zerbi, the Englishman has to be picked when fit. Purely because it seems Spurs don't have a choice.

However, whether it be rustiness following his latest setbacks or another reason, Solanke didn't offer anywhere near enough as the number nine. He managed just 19 touches. That's less than Kinsky in goal.

More worryingly, he had zero shots. If the man whose job is to find the net isn't even letting fly at it, no wonder Spurs are struggling in the final third.

Only De Zerbi can answer if the reason for this is because his team-mates aren't utlising him enough, or if Solanke can't be relied upon to be the replacement to Harry Kane. Of course, replacing Kane is practically impossible. But, in the three years since he left for Germany, Solanke is the only one Spurs have splashed the cash on to fill his shoes.

While reinforcements were clearly needed across the pitch after last season, the fact a fitter, more reliable striker wasn't on the agenda is a concern. And it's biting Spurs now. They can't get an improvement until January now, so De Zerbi has to find a way to get Solanke more involved. Callum Bishop

Bournemouth are now the first team to lead in each of their opening four Premier League games of a season and fail to win any of them.

Marco Rose said it was clear after their Newcastle draw that game management was something they needed to remedy. You can't help but feel a touch sympathetic for a side freely creating as they are.

Latest news and rumours: Bournemouth | Brentford

They took 20 shots with 10 being on target, while Brentford only tested Dorde Petrovic's goal twice. You'd expect two goals in the game off those statistics alone.

The concern will be the speed at which they allowed Brentford back in though.

Against Brentford, they went 2-1 up and conceded again within three minutes. Brentford didn't have to wait long to find a way back into the game, and that's becoming the recurring theme for Bournemouth.

There's clearly enough in this team to win football matches. But until they can control those periods after scoring, and prevent opponents from immediately regaining momentum, they're going to keep leaving points on the table.

Four games, four leads, no wins. Welcome to the Premier League, Marco Rose. William Bitibiri

When they first returned to the Premier League in 2024/25, it was 16 games before Ipswich had recorded two wins.

This time around, it has taken just four.

They beat Sunderland on the opening day, took the lead against Man Utd at Old Trafford the following week - before an eventual 5-2 defeat - and recorded a higher xG than Liverpool in the 2-0 loss last time out.

And against Crystal Palace, both Emersonn and Leif Davis' headers were all too easy. Axel Disasi's sending off gave them an extra boost, but they took advantage when opportunities presented themselves.

When Palace's equaliser made it 2-2, they did not go all out, desperate for the winner; they just waited, exercising patience, with the belief the winner would come, which it eventually did.

While taking three points at Selhurst Park was impressive, equally - if not more so - was the fact it was the third time in the four games they have played that they have conceded less than 0.70 xG.

Fellow newly-promoted side Hull are taking all the plaudits for their start on their return to the Premier League, and rightly so - but, out of the spotlight, Ipswich are going well, too. Dan Long

Aston Villa managed just seven shots against Nottingham Forest. That is the third-lowest shot count they have posted in 59 home league games under Unai Emery.

It wasn't just that Villa failed to score more than once. It was the manner of their attacking play. Everything looked difficult. There was a lack of fluency, a lack of penetration and a lack of ideas.

Villa have undergone significant change this summer and it takes time for new players to understand each other's movements, particularly in the final third. There is also a new goalkeeper behind them and fresh faces still adapting to Emery's demands.

Seven shots at home is a red flag though, regardless of the personnel.

Villa need to find ways of getting their attacking players into dangerous positions more frequently. The worrying thing is that Forest didn't need to produce a defensive masterclass to restrict them.

Of course, Unai Emery is one of the best coaches around at solving problems. He will know this is one that needs addressing quickly. Lewis Jones

The one who bullied defenders at Ipswich. The one who made centre-backs uncomfortable simply by running towards them. The one who plays football like a battering ram.

There was something wonderfully uncomplicated about his performance in Nottingham Forest's 2-1 victory at Aston Villa.

Delap ran the channels relentlessly, chased lost causes and gave Villa's defenders absolutely no time to settle. He was aggressive without being reckless and looked like he was enjoying himself.

He took aim and unleashed a strike that flew into the net with the sort of power that summed up his afternoon perfectly.

That is what Forest signed him for. Lewis Jones

articles.title: El Barcelona rompe la resistencia rojiblanca
articles.standfirst: El doblete de Brugts y los goles de Vicky y Graham firman una trabajada victoria ante el Atlético de Madrid
articles.summary: El doblete de Brugts y los goles de Vicky y Graham firman una trabajada victoria ante el Atlético de Madrid
articles.body: El Barcelona se impuso al Atlético de Madrid (4-2) en el estadio Johan Cruyff en un partido de ida y vuelta en el que el doblete de Brugts y los goles de Vicky y Graham anularon los de Poljak y Jensen, dejando los tres puntos en casa y mantienen a las azulgrana en el liderato una jornada más. Romeu y González tuvieron que lidiar con las numerosas bajas de sus equipos para confeccionar dos onces, sin embargo, de garantías. Partido animoso y con ritmo desde el pitido inicial, fueron las azulgrana las que tuvieron la primera ocasión de peligro. Un centro desde la diestra de Graham que en el intento de despejar de Xènia rebotó en Pajor y obligó a una exhibición de reflejos a Lola, que atajaría en tres tiempos. Poco después, en una contra bien trenzada, llegó el gol del Atlético. El pase filtrado de Fiamma entre las dos centrales lo aprovechó Poljak para definir el mano a mano con Cata con un derechazo ajustado al palo. Marcar tan pronto antes del Barcelona supone todo un ejercicio de supervivencia. El Atlético de Madrid, aun sin querer, se fue echando atrás, regalando espacio y posesión a un equipo, el azulgrana, que pisó el acelerador para buscar el empate. Pina por el interior, Graham por la derecha, Pajor como referencia en punta. Se echó de menos algo más de Kerolin, gran fichaje del verano y ‘perdida’ en esta ocasión ubicada en el extremo zurdo. El empate llegaría pasado el ecuador del primer acto con un pase de Graham y ejecución de primeras de Vicky llegando desde atrás. Las visitantes al vendaval, estiraron sus posesiones y plantaron batalla en el poblado centro del campo. La calma tensa se rompió en el tiempo de añadido del primer acto, primero con una doble ocasión del Barcelona que desbarataron Lola y Xènia en línea de gol y una contra de manual en la que el Atlético pidió penalti por falta de Kerolin sobre Luany, pero que Lorena Trujillano, tras consultar en el FVS, decidió no pitar. El Barcelona completó la remontada en el arranque del segundo acto, en un córner sacado en corto y que acabó con un centro de Pina y un cabezazo de Brugts, sola, colando el balón por debajo de las piernas de Lola. La respuesta del Atlético fue casi inmediata. Un pase filtrado de Poljak sobre Lucía acabó en asistencia para Jensen, que superó a Cata con un toque sutil. Pasada la hora de juego, el Barcelona volvió a nivelar la balanza de su parte. Pina, de nuevo ejerciendo de asistente, puso un balón preciso, con la zurda y desde el costado izquierdo, para que Graham la empujara en el lado opuesto. El Atlético tuvo el empate en las botas de Csiszár, a quien Cata sacó un mano a mano. A diez minutos para el final, Lola tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego lesionada y debutó con las rojiblancas Génesis. A falta de tres minutos para el final llegó la sentencia en un córner botado por Vicky y rematado por Brugts a la jaula.

articles.title: Jhon Lucumí hace una dura autocrítica de la Selección: "Puede sonar a que somos mediocres"
articles.standfirst: Jhon Lucumí frena la euforia en la Selección Colombia
articles.summary: Jhon Lucumí frena la euforia en la Selección Colombia
articles.body: El defensor central de la Selección Colombia, Jhon Janer Lucumí, ofreció un análisis sincero e introspectivo sobre la participación de la 'Tricolor' en la Copa del Mundo 2026. En medio del balance de lo sucedido en el certamen orbital, el flamante zaguero de la Juventus reconoció la complejidad de calificar la actuación del equipo sin caer en el conformismo, pero defendió los progresos futbolísticos del grupo. Durante su intervención en el programa El Vbar de Caracol Radio, Lucumí expresó que el balance del Mundial le genera sentimientos encontrados. Por un lado, está la frustración colectiva de no haber alcanzado la meta planteada; por el otro, la certeza de que el rendimiento deportivo mostró pasajes de alto nivel. "Decir que el Mundial de Colombia fue positivo puede sonar a que somos mediocres o nos conformamos con lo que pasó, pero no es así. Es una sensación 50/50, porque el objetivo principal no se logró, pero en muchos aspectos se consiguieron cosas positivas", aseguró el zaguero caleño. Lucumí enfatizó que el plantel compartía el mismo sentimiento de insatisfacción que la afición al quedar eliminados frente a Suiza, pues dentro del vestuario existía el convencimiento de que el equipo estaba para llegar mucho más lejos. "Nos vimos bien y lo que le pasaba a la gente nos pasaba a nosotros: pensábamos que estábamos para mucho más. No fuimos inferiores a nadie", agregó. Pese al trago amargo, el defensor respaldó el proceso de adaptación y consolidación que vive el combinado nacional. Para Lucumí, las altas expectativas que hoy rodean a la 'Tricolor' son muestra del salto de calidad que se ha dado en los últimos años. "Cada vez estamos mucho más cerca de conseguir un título. Vamos por muy buen camino. Si ves años atrás, cada vez la gente habla más de ganar títulos y si lo hacen es porque tenemos los fundamentos para lograrlo", sentenció. Las declaraciones de Lucumí llegan en un momento cumbre de su carrera profesional. Tras sus destacadas actuaciones con el Bologna y su desempeño en el Mundial, el defensor dio un paso clave al fichar por la Juventus de Turín, donde ya suma minutos como titular en la Serie A de Italia. Con este recorrido en la élite europea, Lucumí se proyecta como una de las voces de liderazgo en la zaga defensiva de la Selección Colombia de cara a los próximos retos internacionales.

articles.title: Julián Alvarez enciende las alarmas
articles.standfirst: El argentino tiene difícil jugar en Anoeta tras retirarse de la última sesión de entrenamiento por problemas físicos, apuntando a una enfermería en la que ya están Sorloth y Barrios
articles.summary: El argentino tiene difícil jugar en Anoeta tras retirarse de la última sesión de entrenamiento por problemas físicos, apuntando a una enfermería en la que ya están Sorloth y Barrios
articles.body: Tras un mes sin poder contar con Sorloth y después del batacazo que supone la lesión de Barrios en el sóleo, la situación médica aún se complica más en el Atlético: Julián Alvarez también apunta a la enfermería. Así se desprende de la retirada del delantero de la última sesión de entrenamiento, después incluso de que formara como titular en la prueba de cara a la Real Sociedad. Aquejado de unos problemas físicos, la Araña no podría acabar junto a sus compañeros, quedando ahora a la espera de una exploración más exhaustiva que determine el alcance de su dolencia. Pero por lo pronto, su presencia en Anoeta se antoja muy difícil. Cabe recordar que Julián disputó los 90 minutos en la visita al Liverpool del pasado miércoles por primera vez en la temporada, tras una puesta a punto que estuvo condicionada tanto por el culebrón protagonizado con su futuro como por su regreso tardío a los entrenamientos (el 10 de agosto) y la 'indisposición' que le impidió trabajar con el grupo durante prácticamente una semana. Precisamente ahora, una vez que cerrado el mercado Julián había asumido su continuidad con el propósito de volver a ser el que era y ganarse el 'perdón' de su afición a base de goles, estos problemas médicos suponen todo un frenazo a su 'reinserción' en el equipo. De hecho, tras mostrar un gesto más alegre y despachar una buena actuación en Anfield saldada con la asistencia a Llorente y un gran disparo que exigió un paradón de Alisson, ya se aguardaba su primer gol antes de volver a jugar en el Metropolitano, pero parece que ahora tendrá que esperar.

articles.title: Liverpool 0-0 Fulham: More dropped points at Anfield - is it too early for Liverpool to worry?
articles.summary: Liverpool have failed to win either of their first two Premier League games at Anfield. But is it too early to worry?
articles.body:
Two Premier League matches at Anfield. Two draws.

For just the third time in 63 years, Liverpool have failed to win either of their opening home games of a league season - not exactly the flying start new boss Andoni Iraola would have been dreaming of.

After such an encouraging midweek performance against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, full of urgency, Saturday's goalless draw against Fulham was a flat follow-up, especially with the Cottagers lacking in confidence and having conceded seven goals in their first three league games.

The Reds looked physically and mentally tired and, to put it bluntly, like an entirely different team to the one that won against a Diego Simeone side that made it to the Champions League semi-finals last season.

On the first real look at how Iraola's style will cope with two games a week, this was certainly not what the Liverpool head coach, nor the Anfield crowd, would have wanted to see.

Former boss Jurgen Klopp would often speak about recognising his team based on their identity and intensity rather than just their colours and judging by Iraola's words since he took over, the Spaniard wants the same too.

Iraola said: "What was lacking was quite clear, it is the first game we had problems to create chances and score goals and make the difference offensively, and that is the main reason we couldn't create chances."

His side are still unbeaten and it is hardly a crisis, but he will look at a return of six points from their first four Premier League games as disappointing, particularly by dropping four points at home to Nottingham Forest and Fulham , with another draw coming at Newcastle and their sole success at Ipswich.

Keeper Alisson told Sky Sports: "We are not happy at all with the draw. It is not something that should happen with Liverpool . To be unbeaten, but with three draws, is not something to celebrate too much with this shirt.

"If we want to do something special [this season] we have to cope with playing a game Wednesday, Saturday and then Tuesday.

"We need to have the right mental state and that was not the case from what we showed. Inside we have it, but we have to just put it out and put more energy on the pitch."

The £364m attacking trio of Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz started together for the first time in a league game and although Liverpool had decent chances, they created nowhere near enough.

Isak's 16 touches in 90 minutes was the second fewest for an outfield Reds player on record, having had the fewest (14) against Forest a fortnight ago.

German Wirtz looked a shadow of the player who was terrific in midweek against Atleti and while Barcola and Isak had a few encouraging moments, that is a partnership that will take time to develop.

"Bradley is one we are building up physically with games and the games will give him the condition we want," Iraola told Match of the Day.

"But it is not just Bradley, we lack the freshness. I only remember one clear chance [for Fulham ] and we kept the structure but offensively we need to do much better."

Frustrated Liverpool held as Fulham pick up first point

'There is a lack of freshness - we cannot hide it'

Before the game against Atletico Madrid, Iraola was asked about how he sought to strike the right balance, with the intensity levels he craves and such a busy schedule.

His response was he didn't want his players to save energy because they had another game in three days.

"You play 55 minutes for me and you are dead and ask for a sub, then perfect," said Iraola. "We have a top-level 55 minutes and then a top-level 35 minutes."

By the hour mark against Fulham , all three of Iraola's changes to the starting line-up were replaced, with left-back Kostas Tsimikas taken off at half-time and Ryan Gravenberch and Victor Munoz replaced after 60 minutes.

Despite sending on Milos Kerkez, Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister, Rio Ngumoha and Jeremie Frimpong, Liverpool showed little improvement.

Iraola admitted: "The players were tired and there is a lack of freshness - we cannot hide it. This is the worst turnaround in terms of 60 or 70 hours [since the last game], but this is going to happen in the season and we have to adapt and it is these kind of games that you need to win sometimes with a set-play or a moment of brilliance."

It is still early, but already there is a realisation from Iraola and his players that when they have such short turnarounds between games, perhaps it is a case of adapting and finding ways to get a result.

With at least seven more Champions League games to follow and a Carabao Cup tie at home to Tottenham on Tuesday, Liverpool must adapt sooner rather than later as the fixture list cranks up if they are to show they can challenge for honours this season.

articles.title: Anselmi: "Jugando así seremos un equipo duro"
articles.standfirst: El técnico, positivo tras el resultado y la imagen ofrecida ante el Athletic
articles.summary: El técnico, positivo tras el resultado y la imagen ofrecida ante el Athletic
articles.body: El técnico del Elche, Martín Anselmi, vio positivo el punto sacado por su equipo en la visita a San Mamés y destacó la imagen de sus jugadores: "Orgulloso de mis jugadores. Teníamos claro que había que competir diferente y hoy hemos demostrado que así seremos un equipo muy duro". "Competimos, venir aquí y competir de esta forma, luchando por cada bola, sufriendo cuando había que hacerlo y jugar cuando pudimos... trabajando juntos, que es lo más importante". "Siempre que estás ganando quieres llevarte los tres puntos. Me gustaría ver la jugada del gol, para tenerla más clara. Para verla de vuelta". "Entendí que al intervalo había que empezar a presionar. Ya habíamos cumplido el objetivo al descanso. Conseguimos darles menos tiempo en el segundo tiempo. El penal llegó a través de una presión. Nos terminan hundiendo, perdimos el mediocampo y por eso quisimos cambiar la línea de cuatro. Perseguíamos mucho, no estábamos teniendo mediocampo. Al final es una jugada individual la que genera el empate". "El equipo merecía más antes. Mereció otra cosa ante la Real, no sé si con Racing. Con el Dépor podíamos haber ganado... los puntos son los que te dan la recompensa del esfuerzo. Hacer esfuerzo sin recompensa es duro".

articles.summary: Akron's coaching staff had a unique addition to start the team's clash with Robert Morris on Saturday.
articles.body:
Akron's coaching staff had a unique addition to start the team's clash with Robert Morris on Saturday.

The Zips previously held an "Offensive Coordinator of the Game" promotion , as season-ticker holder Martin Allan Whims II received the opportunity to script their opening drive of Saturday's contest alongside head coach Joe Moorhead.

Here's how each play of the drive unfolded.

Realistic Upsets That Would Send the Season into Chaos 😲

12-yard rush by running back Jordan Gant

Two-yard pass from quarterback Cibastian Broughton to receiver Kyan Mason

Seven-yard rush by running back Jordan Gant

Marcel Williams fumble following a seven-yard pass from quarterback Cibastian Broughton

While the drive ended in a turnover, it was hardly the fault of the temporary offensive coordinator.

It was a commendable effort from Whims, as Akron was on the verge of picking up its second first down of the drive to advance deeper in Robert Morris' territory before the fumble occurred.

Prior to the game, Whims detailed his reaction to finding out that he won the play-calling contest.

"There's celebrities out there that bought 18 season tickets," Whims said, per SI.com's Patrick Andres . "You don't think your one entry's gonna be good enough to win it all. Just complete and utter shock and excitement—it's been quite the ride the past couple weeks since I found out I was a winner."

The Zips entered Saturday's action looking to improve to 1-1, as they suffered a 38-16 loss to Wake Forest in their season-opener on Sept. 3. While Akron hasn't posted a winning record since 2015, the team's win total has increased in each of the past two years under Moorhead.

"We're definitely at a point where I feel like we're starting to turn a corner, over the past couple years," Whims said, per Andres. "Hopefully we can get [to six wins] this year and maybe make it to a bowl game again."

Despite the opening-drive fumble, Akron held a 7-0 lead over Robert Morris at the end of the first quarter.

articles.title: Bryce Underwood, John Mateer's Box Score Stats, Highlights, Draft Stock from Oklahoma vs. Michigan
articles.summary: The third all-time meeting between Oklahoma and Michigan turned into a defensive slugfest with the Wolverines prevailing 17-10 at the Big House.
articles.body:
The third all-time meeting between Oklahoma and Michigan turned into a defensive slugfest with the Wolverines prevailing 17-10 at the Big House.

A once-anticipated quarterback showdown between Bryce Underwood and John Mateer failed to live up to any hype it might have had.

Michigan, coming off one of the most controversial wins in college football history, came out this week looking like it wanted to send a message after falling out of the AP Top 25 poll with a 91-yard touchdown drive in the first quarter.

Underwood showed off his athletic ability on that scoring drive with a 38-yard run to find the end zone.

The Wolverines added a field goal late in the second quarter to take a 10-0 lead before the offense stalled.

Oklahoma came back in the third quarter with its first scoring drive. Mateer went 5-of-5 for 77 yards on the drive, capped off by Mackenzie Alleyne's 22-yard touchdown catch.

That was the peak of Mateer's performance. Michigan cornerback Jyaire Hill undercut a third-down pass from Mateer in the fourth quarter for an interception, Jordan Marshall's one-yard touchdown run two plays later with 7:53 remaining turned out to be the difference in the game.

Mateer and Underwood were both under the microscope as fans and analysts took stock of their performances:

Given how negative the discussion around Michigan was coming out of the Western Michigan game, head coach Kyle Whittingham is breathing a huge sigh of relief.

The Wolverines could find themselves back in the top 25 next week now that they are 2-0 with a quality win under their belt. They still have a long way to go before looking like an elite program, but this was exactly what they needed to happen.

On the other side of the equation, Brent Venables' seat that seemed like it cooled off after getting a six-year extension last month might be warming up again.

Mateer's 2025 season was disrupted by a thumb injury required surgery, so it was assumed a full offseason would get him back on track. This game just looked like more of the same from the fifth-year senior with one terrific drive, but nothing great around it to help lift his team in a hostile road environment.

Oklahoma will try to rebound at home next week against New Mexico before a brutal two-game stretch against Georgia and Texas. Michigan will stay home next weekend to host UTEP as it looks to start 3-0 for the first time since 2023.

articles.title: Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways including West Ham looking ominous
articles.summary: BBC Final Score pundit Sam Parkin looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including West Ham and Swansea.
articles.body:
With five weeks gone of the EFL season, Final Score pundit and former Swindon, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker Sam Parkin selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

West Ham are really hitting their stride and have surged to the top of the Championship after winning their last four matches, including walloping Wrexham 6-0 on Friday.

Parkin: "They've scored 20 goals in just seven games and their attacking players are coming to the fore.

"In the early part of the season, they probably had a few defensive issues and their forward players papered over the cracks to a certain degree, but on Friday night it all came together.

"Jarrod Bowen said after the game how important it was to get the transfer window closed so you know exactly who's going to be there.

"Ultimately when you can get Manor Solomon, Jarrod Bowen, Valentin Castellanos and Joel Piroe in the same Championship side, they're going to cause havoc.

"Those were the ingredients on Friday night. Wrexham were bad, but I don't think we should get too carried away by Wrexham's performance when you consider the embarrassment of riches that West Ham have got.

"It's looking pretty ominous already for the rest of the Championship when you consider the amount of goals they've scored across the last four games."

Vitor Matos' Swansea City remain second behind West Ham on goal difference after beating Burnley 3-1 on Saturday, a fourth win this season.

Parkin: "Swansea have made an amazing start to the season. It's important to have both centre-forwards scoring and both Zan Vipotnik and Adam Idah scored against Burnley.

"They've got strength in depth there. They've made some really interesting signings from different leagues, which you always expect from Swansea, going back over the years.

"I mentioned Stephen Welsh on Final Score and the centre-half was an interesting buy from Celtic. He's really hit the ground running and I think their main strength is their defending, which maybe is not something you always associate with Swansea.

"But four clean sheets already this season shows you that they've got the balance right between defence and attack.

"Can they make a fist at getting automatically promoted? I doubt it, but with the extension to the play-offs, they can fight and win a place in the top eight. That would definitely be a realistic ambition for them."

Stockport win must be a turning point for Leicester

Leicester City and manager Russell Martin got a very welcome win at Stockport County on Saturday after the low of losing 4-0 at home to Oxford last weekend.

Parkin: "Stockport was a really difficult game in the aftermath of losing 4-0 at home to Oxford. That was a real low for the supporters, so it was an enormous game on Saturday.

"The victory is all important and it doesn't really matter how it came. Yes, there will be people picking holes in the result and saying they conceded three goals, but Stockport have been there or thereabouts for a number of seasons.

"You can see a little sprinkling of real experience in Leicester now. Emil Riis was the difference against Stockport with his two goals and he is vastly experienced from his time in the Championship.

"John Lundstram, another scorer at Stockport, is also vastly experienced as is Liam Cullen, who got the other goal. He was a trusted player for Russell Martin previously at Swansea.

"Those are three guys with loads of experience in the second tier. The young lads at Leicester are being thrown into a really-difficult situation and they're going to need those three.

"Leicester and Martin will hope Stockport is a springboard because it's no good if they lose the next game and they are back where they started."

Barnet can get in the play-offs under Brennan

Barnet under Dean Brennan are top of League Two following their win against Accrington Stanley and they are unbeaten in their first six league games.

Parkin: "Dean celebrates five years at Barnet this month and he's done it the hard way.

"He's managed in non-league, well below National League level. He had a brilliantly-entertaining side and he's continued that in the EFL.

"Barnet are free scoring under him and they scored another two at Accrington.

"Charlie Lakin has been a bit of a revelation for them and he's scored five goals already from midfield. He wasn't free scoring by any stretch when he was at Walsall previously.

"Dean's teams are always a good watch, always very entertaining. You have to get the balance right in League Two, between being able to get points on the road and being attacking at home. I think he's getting that balance right.

"They're much fancied this season and I would be really confident they can emulate last season's really strong finish and get in the play-offs this time round."

Walsall changing their style under Grant

Walsall hope they can make it third time lucky in winning promotion from League Two after their heartbreaks over the past two years and they are unbeaten so far under Lee Grant.

Parkin: "Walsall are a really interesting case of a side who are changing their style.

"They had real success over the first two halves of the last two seasons under Mat Sadler. Mat had a real fixed way of playing that was getting success, but they just couldn't sustain it to get over the line.

"Walsall fans will be treated to a different brand of play and they had 70% possession against Rochdale on Saturday.

"Defensively they are very solid and have four clean sheets in their six league games. They've only conceded four times and have the joint-best defence in League Two.

"They've been blessed in the past with good forwards, such as Freddie Draper and Nathan Lowe, but they still had 24 shots against Rochdale, despite not scoring, and their goalkeeper made six saves.

"They've made a really good start and I'm sure the supporters are encouraged that they could go one better and get promoted this season."

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's David Anderson.
