articles.title: Tottenham 0-0 Everton: Spurs remain winless and goalless in Premier League as Toffees stay unbeaten goalless after another bore draw against Everton
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Tottenham remain winless and goalless in Premier League this season with 0-0 draw against Everton; first time Spurs have failed to score in any of their first four league games of a season; Spurs booed off at full-time as Toffees maintain unbeaten start
articles.body:
It is the first time Spurs have failed to score in any of their first four league games of a season, while it is now over 400 minutes since their last Premier League goal.

Following last weekend's goalless draw at Nottingham Forest, it was another toothless display from Roberto De Zerbi's new-look, expensively assembled side, who were booed off at the full-time whistle.

Latest news and rumours: Tottenham | Everton

A disgruntled home crowd watched their side have just two shots on target - the first a weak second-half effort from Mateus Fernandes met with ironic cheers - create one big chance and register a paltry expected goals of 0.64.

Everton had the better moments to earn their first away league win since February, but ex-Spurs winger Brennan Johnson blazed a great second-half chance over, while earlier, Spurs goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky nearly gifted Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall an opener.

The Toffees weathered Spurs' early storm as the home side had four shots in the opening 10 minutes, with Jan Paul van Hecke missing a great close-range chance.

But the defender's fifth-minute effort proved to be Tottenham's best opportunity as De Zerbi's side became the first Spurs team to go on a four-game goalless run in 20 years.

It was also the first goalless draw at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in the Premier League (140th game), and the first time that Spurs have drawn 0-0 in a home game in the competition since September 2017.

Redknapp: Spurs' goalless run 'absolutely diabolical'

"After spending £300m, I didn't think there would be a problem scoring goals. But to not score in six hours of football is absolutely diabolical.

"For the first 20 minutes, I thought that this is what I want to see. There was a moment when Fernandes had a shot and the whole crowd celebrated. It's not great.

"The connection with the fans and the players is not there. I don't know when they are going to get their first win. It might go on for longer, but I do still see some positives.

"It cannot stay this way with what is at their disposal. There are things that I don't like. Robertson was your left-back and your wide left player because Marmoush wanted to come inside. That balance didn't really work, so you are lopsided with what you're trying to do.

"Trying to get the best squad is what De Zerbi has to solve. The midfield balance also isn't right. You've got to find a way of getting a Kudus into the ten, or Maddison if he gets fit. I'm not sure how Kulusevski's going to be but when he's fit you've got to get him in.

"Even I'm looking and thinking 'how would I change it?' There are more questions than answers. He tried everything today. He couldn't find it. The quality wasn't there, but they have got quality players."

De Zerbi was involved in an exchange at full-time on the pitch with Mathys Tel, who was brought on as a second-half substitute.

The Italian explained at his post-match press conference: "I coached him on the pitch. The body shape: he's a striker; the striker can't play with the shoulder on the goal.

"If we are playing with (James) Maddison, (Mohammed) Kudus and Savio, he has to play as a striker, and the striker has to look at the goal, or for the cross of (Andy) Robertson. He has to stay inside.

"He started as a striker; now he's playing as a winger, but he started his career as a striker.

"But I love Mathys as a player, as a guy; that is not a problem."

Moyes pleased with Toffees' resilience but wanted more

"I wanted much more from the team, but I told them about coming here.

"We've not had a great record here. Only a couple months ago we missed out on Europe here. I generally felt that we had to come here and show a bit more.

"Tottenham were so good for 20 minutes. They put us under so much pressure. We found it difficult to escape from it. We created a couple chances ourselves, but we didn't play well enough today when we had the ball.

"We know exactly where we're short and what we could do better at and what we'd like to do better. But there'll be some games where we might have to play that way just to get ourselves through. It wasn't the plan, we were forced into it by Tottenham. I thought we did a really good job of being resilient."

5: SPURS GO CLOSE! Jan Paul van Hecke puts over Andy Robertson's free-kick from close range.

45+1: KINSKY SAVES! The first shot on target of the game is produced by Everton's James Garner from a long-range free-kick, which is palmed away by Antonin Kinsky.

HALF TIME: No shot on target for Tottenham, who fail to score in the first half for a 26th Premier League game since the start of last season.

47: FIRST SPURS SHOT ON TARGET! Mateus Fernandes' weak low shot is straight at Jordan Pickford, but it brings ironic cheers from the Spurs fans.

50: KINSKY SAVES! Thierno Barry's back-post header is saved by Kinsky, who didn't know much about it.

66: KINSKY GETS LUCKY! The Spurs goalkeeper passes it straight to Dewsbury-Hall but he hits his shot straight at Kinsky.

89: FROM ZERO TO HERO FOR PICKFORD! The Everton goalkeeper gives the ball away to allow Lucas Bergvall a shot, which he superbly saves.

Millions spent, but where is the goalscorer?

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

"It doesn't take a genius to figure out where Tottenham's biggest concern lies right now. You can't win games if you don't score goals. That's why Spurs haven't won a league game this season, after going 400 minutes without finding the net.

"They have so many creative players, all of whom were on the pitch against the Toffees. Yet the man who they need to score the bulk of their goals was anonymous. Or at the very least, wasn't found.

"Dominic Solanke's fitness for Tottenham feels imperative. As the only out and out number nine available to De Zerbi, the Englishman has to be picked when fit. Purely because it seems Spurs don't have a choice.

"However, whether it be rustiness following his latest setbacks or another reason, Solanke didn't offer anywhere near enough as the number nine. He managed just 19 touches. That's less than Kinsky in goal.

"More worryingly, he had zero shots. If the man whose job is to find the net isn't even letting fly at it, no wonder Spurs are struggling in the final third.

"Only De Zerbi can answer if the reason for this is because his team-mates aren't utlising him enough, or if Solanke can't be relied upon to be the replacement to Harry Kane. Of course, replacing Kane is practically impossible. But, in the three years since he left for Germany, Solanke is the only one Spurs have splashed the cash on to fill his shoes.

"While reinforcements were clearly needed across the pitch after last season, the fact a fitter, more reliable striker wasn't on the agenda is a concern. And it's biting Spurs now. They can't get an improvement until January now, so De Zerbi has to find a way to get Solanke more involved."

articles.title: Siete años sin ganar al Atlético en LaLiga
articles.standfirst: La Real no supera a los de Simeone en el torneo de la regularidad desde el 14 de septiembre de 2019, con ocho derrotas y cinco empates desde entonces
articles.summary: La Real no supera a los de Simeone en el torneo de la regularidad desde el 14 de septiembre de 2019, con ocho derrotas y cinco empates desde entonces
articles.body: La Real se agarra a la victoria en la tanda de penaltis de la Copa para pensar que puede superar al Atlético esta noche en LaLiga, algo que no logra desde el 14 de septiembre de 2019, hace ya por tanto siete años, cuando se impuso por 2-0, con goles de Martin Odegaard y Nacho Monreal. Desde entonces, el balance en el torneo de la regularidad es de ocho victorias rojiblancas, tres de ellas en San Sebastián, y cinco empates. Sólo Igor Zubeldia, baja de última hora por unas molestias, y Mikel Oyarzabal, que fueron titulares, y Álex Remiro, que estuvo en un banquillo al que parece apunta esta vez también, permanecen en la plantilla de la Real de aquel último triunfo liguero frente al Atlético, habiendo vencido después al resto de clubes de Primera, Real Madrid y Barcelona incluidos. Cabe reseñar también en favor de los realistas al hablar de este duelo liguero que salvo un 4-0 y dos 0-2, el resto de los partidos que han perdido frente a los colchoneros han sido por la mínima. Hay, eso sí, otro triunfo realista desde ese 14 de septiembre de 2019, además del del 18 de abril de este 2026, y se dio también en el torneo del K.O., cuando en enero de 2022 los hoy locales se impusieron por 2-0 en la ronda de octavos de final.

articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC vs. East TN St. Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Led by head coach Bill Belichick, the North Carolina Tar Heels improved to 2-0 on the season with a 35-3 victory over the East Tennessee State Buccaneers in their home opener at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, on Saturday.
articles.body:
Led by head coach Bill Belichick, the North Carolina Tar Heels improved to 2-0 on the season with a 35-3 victory over the East Tennessee State Buccaneers in their home opener at Kenan Stadium in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, on Saturday.

UNC entered the game as a 35.5-point favorite , and it was clearly the better team throughout thanks largely to the play of quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. and running back Demon June.

Here is a look at the Tar Heels' top statistical performers from Saturday's win:

Edwards and the UNC offense came out firing on Saturday, scoring three touchdowns on five first-half drives.

Two of those first-half touchdowns came courtesy of Edwards, who hit tight end Jelani Thurman for a 24-yard score and running back Benjamin Hall for a 26-yard touchdown:

June closed out the scoring for North Carolina in the first half with a nine-yard rushing touchdown, and he followed that up with six- and one-yard scores in the third quarter:

All told, the North Carolina offense piled up 427 total yards and 23 first downs.

Belichick's defensive unit was just as good, allowing 255 total yards and forcing two turnovers.

It wasn't a surprising result Saturday given that ETSU is an FCS team, but it was an encouraging performance for UNC nonetheless.

North Carolina disappointed in its first season under Belichick in 2025, finishing just 4-8. However, the Tar Heels are off to a much better start so far this season.

In addition to their drubbing of ETSU, the Tar Heels kicked off their 2026 campaign with a 15-10 win over TCU in Dublin, Ireland, in Week 0.

The level of competition is about to get much tougher for North Carolina and its six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach, though.

Next week, the Tar Heels will head to South Carolina for a road game against the Clemson Tigers, followed by a home date with the No. 3 Notre Dame Fighting Irish on Oct. 3.

articles.title: Rangers v Celtic: What makes Sunday's League Cup quarter-final crucial?
articles.summary: BBC Scotland previews the first meeting of Rangers and Celtic this season as the Old Firm rivals prepare to face off in the Premier Sports Cup quarter-finals.
articles.body:
No away fans, calamities in Europe and Derek McInnes' Old Firm debut as a manager.

In Glasgow, every Old Firm match is big, but going into Sunday there is a sense this game could be seismic.

Rangers legend Graeme Souness says the Premier Sports Cup quarter-final is an opportunity for both sides to "put a marker down" as they meet for the first time this season.

But what can we expect as Rangers and Celtic face off (12:00 BST) at Ibrox?

Celtic have won all six of their Scottish Premiership matches so far this season with 14 goals scored and just three conceded, but that does not quite tell the full story.

They squeezed past Dundee at home in their first game of the season, but that was followed by rampant wins at Kilmarnock and Dundee United.

Things looked even better when they put three goals past LASK without response in the first leg of their Champions League play-off, but what occurred the following week was a capitulation of the highest order.

Callum McGregor's early goal in Austria had Celtic four goals to the good and heading for the league phase, but LASK mounted the comeback of all comebacks to win 5-1 on the night and 5-4 on aggregate.

While the ship has steadied since then and Celtic have won all four of their following league matches, a narrow victory at St Johnstone in midweek was far from convincing, albeit manager Martin O'Neill had made significant changes to his starting line-up.

Previewing Sunday's derby encounter, Celtic great Scott Brown explained the importance of a fast start in this fixture.

"As a Celtic player, you want to silence that crowd early doors," he said.

"You want to make sure that you keep the ball, you dictate, and if Celtic get an early goal it becomes a nervous Ibrox.

"The big [derby] is always the first game."

For Rangers, domestically, it's been a different story. They began the new season with a draw at Dundee United and a defeat to Hibernian, leaving McInnes winless in his first two Premiership matches as manager.

But a rampant League Cup win against St Mirren, followed by four league wins on the bounce, and things look a bit rosier heading into Sunday's game at Ibrox.

While things have improved domestically, McInnes' men faced similar embarrassment to their city rivals on the European stage.

After finishing third in the league last term, they entered the Europa League third qualifying round.

Rangers were beaten 2-1 by Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok in the first leg and their 1-1 draw at home meant they dropped into the Conference League play-offs.

The first leg of that tie was played in Glasgow, where McInnes' men were 1-0 winners against Czech side Jablonec , who ultimately won on penalties in the return leg .

Earlier this month, it was confirmed there would be no away supporters at any SPFL matches between the city rivals this season.

The "temporary arrangement" was reached following talks between the Glasgow clubs and the SPFL and follows the Scottish FA's independent review into events surrounding last term's Scottish Cup quarter-final at Ibrox , which was marred by unrest and pitch incursions from both sets of fans.

About 8,000 visiting fans, a figure that was much larger than previous away allocations, had been allowed into Ibrox back in March to witness Celtic's penalty shootout win.

The disorder that followed prompted the SFA to force both Celtic and Rangers to play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors .

For this weekend's League Cup clash, Rangers had initially proposed an allocation of 300 supporters , but Celtic rejected the offer and in light of the SPFL's ruling, there will be no away fans inside Ibrox on Sunday.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes: "I think we've got to bring the crowd with us.

"You're not going to play Celtic and dominate the game for 90 minutes. We'll have spells, they'll have spells, it's just the way it is.

"I think it's important that we tap into having that 50,000 behind us and be behind the players, support them, have their backs, not be on their backs and really make it as tough for Celtic as possible.

"There's been a lot of frustration over a period of time at the club and it's up to us to try and show that we're going to deliver something a bit different."

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill: "I suppose if you get in front in the game, that makes them anxious.

"Talking about getting in front and getting in front are two different things. The crowd will be right behind their team, which you would expect.

"We just do our best. We know that we're up against a very fine side. We're up against a crowd that can make a difference.

"I'd be delighted to be celebrating something in the game."

Celtic have won the past six League Cup meetings between the clubs since losing the final to Rangers in 2011.

Celtic's last League Cup win at Ibrox was in the groups in 1973. They also beat Rangers in the semis that season but have never won a League Cup knockout tie in Govan.

Celtic have only won four of their previous 14 games against Rangers at Ibrox.

Rangers have only failed to get to the semis once in the past decade.

Celtic haven't lost at the quarter-final stage since 2009, when Hearts beat them 1-0 at Celtic Park thanks to a Michael Stewart penalty - current coach Stephen McManus was sent off late in the tie.

O'Neill's record at Ibrox: played 11, won six, drawn one, lost four.

McInnes' record against Celtic: played 61, won 10, drawn four, lost 47.

articles.title: Tottenham 0-0 Everton: Spurs blanked again as new era turns into a false dawn
articles.summary: Toothless Spurs' draw a blank again and are now in danger of seeing a brave new era turn into a false dawn, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
The banner held aloft by a Tottenham Hotspur supporter before kick-off was not so much a plea for action as a cry for help.

"Please Score A Goal" was the message brandished in the direction of the Spurs players as they came out against Everton in search of their first in the Premier League this season.

After another goalless 45 minutes, there was a compelling case for a hasty rewrite asking "Please Have A Shot" as, for all their possession, Roberto de Zerbi's expensively assembled side struggled to get anywhere near Jordan Pickford's goal.

And so it went on in an increasingly angry and frustrated atmosphere inside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as Spurs' goalless league streak extended to 407 minutes as a stuttering start to what was meant to be brave new era continued.

It was the first time they have failed to score in their opening four league games across all four tiers - and also in four successive Premier League matches since September 2006.

The grim statistic would be bad enough in any circumstances, but it is even worse after Spurs spent in excess of £300m in the summer, much of it designed to give De Zerbi's side an added edge.

This was the first Premier League goalless draw, in the 140th game, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

It may seem early days for an apology to the supporters, but De Zerbi felt the need as he said: "I'm sorry to the fans. We are sorry to the fans.

"They were fantastic, especially in the first part of the game because when they see the team is playing well, pushing to find the solution they were inside the pitch with my players. Then the reaction of the fans is normal. We have to say thanks all the time to them."

Everton could have actually made matters worse, but they are also short of attacking threat themselves - luckily for Spurs.

As the second half wore on, the resilient visitors actually missed the game's two best chances through Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Brennan Johnson, while the mood became increasingly sour as nerves and anxiety grew.

When £85m summer signing Mateus Fernandes had Spurs' first shot on target after 46 minutes, the stadium rattled to the sound of ironic applause.

There was no irony when they played the ball around at the back with only seven minutes left, and when the final whistle sounded it was just like old times - or at least like last season - as jeers sent De Zerbi's players on their way.

He went through the card in an attempt to change this embarrassing barren sequence in front of goal, playing new signings from Manchester City , Omar Marmoush and Savio, in the attacking positions, with Dominic Solanke handed his first league start of the campaign.

As time went on and the tension mounted, Mohammed Kudus and James Maddison were sent on, but it was another substitute, Lucas Bergvall, who almost snatched victory with a late long-range effort, saved by Everton goalkeeper Pickford after he had gifted the Swede possession and an opportunity.

Watching it all from close quarters was a grim-faced Richarlison, the 29-year-old Brazil striker in dispute with the club over the remaining nine months of his contract.

He was left out of De Zerbi's Premier League squad after a proposed deadline-day return to former club Everton collapsed. A switch back to Brazil with Vasco da Gama has also failed to materialise.

Spurs still without a league goal after Everton draw

The 'xG' - expected goals - statistic suggests Spurs should have scored three or four goals this season, but their non-penalty xG per shot this season is just 0.066. It gives them an expected conversion rate of 6.6%.

In layman's terms, it means they are not very good when comes to creating an attacking threat.

De Zerbi, never someone to disguise his emotions, grew more animated and irritated as the game went on, marching on to the pitch at the final whistle for an exchange with substitute Mathys Tel.

When any side embarks on the sort of root and branch revolution the Italian presided over this summer, it is inevitable there will be teething problems and time required for understandings and relationships to form.

And the change is understandable after two successive 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League. Indeed, Spurs' last league goal actually came against Everton on the final day of last season, courtesy of Joao Palhinha.

It kept them in the top flight, allowing them to make a fresh start for this campaign.

De Zerbi, who still has much work to do to rid Spurs of the aftershock of two poor seasons, said: "I think in the first 30 minutes we were very, good but we didn't find a goal. I think in that moment we suffer too much with confidence and this is another important part for us at the moment.

"In the second half, I observed many players had a little less confidence and I don't like this. They have to be happy and understand we are in the right way.

"The players are human and they have emotions and they think with their head. My position is to help them and stay focus on the improvement we have to do. If we play 90 minutes like we did in the first 30 minutes, I think we are going to win many games."

Spurs, however, have a toothlessness that must be a concern. It is certainly one for the supporters who watched their players either take too long over chances or, on many occasions, passed on the responsibility.

They also ran into a rugged Everton defence, with Jarrad Branthwaite magnificent as he stepped up his claims for a place in Thomas Tuchel's next England squad after injury troubles.

For Spurs, however, there were few positives as the wait for a first Premier League win - and goal - this season goes on.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham Says Michigan 'Deserved' Backlash, Clarifies Bryce Underwood Comments
articles.summary: Following the Michigan Wolverines' 17-10 upset win over the No. 11 Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham addressed last week's performance and his comments about quarterback Bryce Underwood's job security.
articles.body:
Following the Michigan Wolverines' 17-10 upset win over the No. 11 Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham addressed last week's performance and his comments about quarterback Bryce Underwood's job security.

Michigan escaped with a 13-12 victory over Western Michigan last week thanks in large part to the officials putting one second back on the clock following an unsuccessful Hail Mary. After being given new life, Underwood hit JJ Buchanan for the game-winning touchdown on a second Hail Mary.

Fans on social media were highly critical of Michigan's showing in that game, as well as the manner in which the officials handled the clock. Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Whittingham noted that he didn't see what was being said about the Wolverines throughout the week, but added, "If we were treated badly, we probably deserved it because we didn't play very well."

Whittingham also responded to a question about his analysis of Underwood last week. After Michigan's narrow win over Western Michigan, Whittingham told reporters Underwood was the starting quarterback "right now," and added, "At some point, we've got to turn a corner."

On Saturday, Whittingham suggested that he wasn't trying to create a quarterback controversy with his comments, telling reporters , "No job is ever etched in stone. ... I don't agree that I opened that can of worms, Bryce is our quarterback."

Following what was a struggle of a freshman season in 2025, Underwood entered the 2026 season with hopes of taking the next step and being a viable starting quarterback in the Big Ten.

Aside from the Hail Mary that almost wasn't, Underwood did not get off to a great start in Week 1, going 12-of-22 for 170 yards with one touchdown and one interception, while also rushing for 47 yards and a score.

Underwood didn't exactly light it up as a passer on Saturday either, going 9-of-17 for 111 yards with no touchdowns, but he did not throw a pick, and he did damage with his legs, rushing for 87 yards and a touchdown.

Above all, Underwood did enough to lead the Wolverines to a victory over a team that reached the College Football Playoff last season and is a threat to do so again this season.

Michigan dropped out of the Associated Press Top 25 following last week's win over Western Michigan, but beating Oklahoma figures to put the Wolverines back in the mix.

It is clear that huge improvements are still needed, particularly on offense, but a 2-0 record with winnable games against UTEP, Iowa and Minnesota on tap the next three weeks is a much better result than most probably expected amid Michigan's poor outing against WMU.

articles.title: Fire at nursing home in Chile kills 16 elderly residents
articles.summary: The facility had faced fines and enforcement proceedings over regulatory violations since 2019.
articles.body:
A fire at a nursing home in southern Chile has killed 16 elderly residents and left others hospitalised.

The blaze broke out late on Friday at the single-storey care home in Pitrufquen, in the Araucania region, about 640km (400 miles) south of the capital, Santiago.

Firefighters extinguished the flames early Saturday.

Twenty-six elderly people were inside the facility when the fire started. Ten survived and were taken to a local hospital, according to the local government. The private facility had previously faced fines and enforcement proceedings for operating outside regulations.

Images posted on social media showed flames engulfing the building overnight, with firefighters using a water hose to battle the blaze.

Municipal authorities expressed their condolences to the families of those who died. Pitrufquen Mayor Jacqueline Romero said municipal health and public safety teams, firefighters, and police were working at the scene and supporting relatives of the victims.

“In February, the municipality had sent a letter specifically calling for an inspection because the facility was not in compliance with regulations – it was subject to sanitary enforcement proceedings,” Romero told local networks.

Firefighters continued removing debris and collapsed corrugated metal roofing on Saturday, while police secured the area.

The cause of the fire is still unknown. Local prosecutor Jorge Granada said investigators were examining the scene and questioning people to determine how the fire began and whether anyone else was involved.

Regional health official Jose Bravo said the facility had a history of regulatory problems, describing it as an unregulated operation that had been subject to administrative proceedings and fines since 2019.

Romero said the municipality had requested an inspection in February after finding that the home was not complying with regulations and was facing sanitary enforcement proceedings.

Chile President Jose Antonio Kast called for the circumstances surrounding the deaths to be fully investigated in a post on X. He also said he had ordered “urgent measures” to assess conditions at nursing homes nationwide and identify changes needed to prevent a similar incident.

This accident comes less than a week after a fire broke out at Chile’s Hotel Alto Nevados, where FIS Masters Alpine Skiing World Cup racers were staying for a preseason training camp.

articles.title: El Arsenal gana una batalla en Sunderland... con Raya como héroe
articles.standfirst: El meta español paró un penalti antes de los tantos de Guimaraes y Saka
articles.summary: El meta español paró un penalti antes de los tantos de Guimaraes y Saka
articles.body: El Arsenal sigue haciendo pleno en la Premier (cuatro de cuatro) tras un triunfo muy trabajado en una auténtica batalla de fútbol en Sunderland, que se saldó finalmente con el triunfo de los vigentes campeones. Aunque los goles del brasileño Bruno Guimaraes y el penalti marcado por Saka en el descuento fueron claves visibles del choque, el héroe del partido fue, una vez más, el portero del Arsenal, el español David Raya. El meta campeón del mundo detuvo un penalti con una parada extraordinaria en el minuto 56, tras lanzamiento de Enzo Le Fee. Dos minutos después llegaría el citado tanto de Bruno Guimaraes (0-1). Fue un partido durísimo, con muchas batallas parciales en el choque y con continuos saques de banda del Sunderland que ponían en aprietos al campeón de la Premier. Uno de los saques propició el penalti luego fallado por el Sunderland. Tras el penalti de Raya, llegó el tanto de Guimaraes (un golazo desde fuera del área) y el penalti final de Saka tras falta de Reinildo, que fue expulsado. Era el 0-2 ya en el descuento. Con este resultado, el Arsenal sigue en lo más alto de la tabla, con cuatro triunfos en cuatro partidos, en los que sólo ha recibido un gol en contra, con Raya como estrella. El único que le puede empatar haciendo pleno es el City, si gana hoy el derbi de Mánchester ante el United.

articles.title: Con Arda se acaban las broncas
articles.standfirst: El turco cierra un partido que el Madrid se complica después de un buen primer tiempo. Los errores de Lejeune castigan a un Rayo de menos a más que descuenta con gol de Camello
articles.summary: El turco cierra un partido que el Madrid se complica después de un buen primer tiempo. Los errores de Lejeune castigan a un Rayo de menos a más que descuenta con gol de Camello
articles.body: El Madrid estropeó una ocasión estupenda para crecer en juego y confianza, propia y de su gente, aunque descubrió un asunto que puede ser relevante en la temporda. Después de un primer tiempo notable, con tres goles que reflejaron la superioridad blanca, en juego y sobre todo en pegada, se dejó ir para consentir la reacción rayista, que de orgullo va sobrado. Así que después de las palmas volvieron los pitos hasta que ingresó Arda Güler. Es capaz de cambiar la cara al Madrid. En Sevilla, a peor cuando se fue. Ante el Rayo, a mejor para acabar con la bronca y cerrar el partido. El turco está ganando las oposiciones a intocable. La consolidación de Arda se produjo en el día elegido para la puesta de largo de Diomande. El fichaje más caro del curso se estrenó en el once titular de un Mourinho que no es devoto de las rotaciones. Lo demuestra su fe inquebrantable en la BMV y Valverde, que no descansan ni a tiros. El marfileño entró en el costado derecho, donde debía mantenerse Brahim o regresar Güler, pero no son de los intocables. Empezó tímido el africano y se fue soltando. Le ayudó un partido que pareció decantado muy pronto. No necesitó el Madrid ni rematar para ponerse por delante. En una internada de Carreras sin aparente relevancia midió mal Lejeune y cometió penalti. Transformó Mbappé, con frialdad, por la derecha. Y tres minutos después, una mala cesión de Lejeune permitió robar a Vini, dejó atrás y Carreras coronó, tras pared de primeras con su socio Kylian. Si el futbolista más veterano y fiable de un equipo como el Rayo comete esos errores queda claro que es un equipo alicaído, mustio y sin hogar donde refugiarse por el capricho de su dueño. Minuto 17 y 2-0. Se avecinaba tormenta. Jugó bien el Madrid con Bernardo en la sala de máquinas, pero la gasolina le dura para lo que le dura. El portugués apareció siempre en la jugada para ofrecerse, así que mezcla bien con Valverde. Pero quien más aprovechó la coyuntura fue Vinicius, que puso voluntad y fútbol. Desde la conducción al minuto que arrancó los primeros aplausos a los pases que generó desde su costado, como el que convirtió Bellingham en el tercero, perfecto en la llegada desde atrás. Jude se esforzó en dar todo el mérito al 7, que volvió a sonreír. Y el Bernabéu también. Será que exige más al árbol que puede dar más frutos. En el juego y en el esfuerzo. Acumuló varias llegadas más antes del descanso el Madrid con alguna parada de mérito del debutante Audero (buena presentación) y un palo de Mbappé. Remate durísimo desde la frontal. Pero el Rayo es dignidad, y pese a la fragilidad emocional tiene argumentos para hacer daño. Por un lado, Camello, que pide selección. Se fabricó un par de acciones, la segunda bien sacada abajo por Courtois. Por otro, un grupo de buenos peloteros como Pedro Díaz, que abrió la función amenazando desde el centro del campo y cerró el primer acto con un disparo extraordinario, caviar para un Courtois estelar. A tal señor, tal honor. Mandó pronto a sus soldados a calentar Mourinho, mediado el primer acto, y aunque no es amigo de cambios rápidos, el calendario aprieta. Entró Camavinga, pero el Madrid regresó desconectado, y el Rayo decidió olvidar el primer tiempo y atreverse. Pedro Díaz conectó otro derechazo imponente que se fue al poste, fruto de la presión rayista. Y fue la persecución de Ratiu la que obligó a arriesgar en la cesión a Vini, la pelota quedó muerta y Sergio Camello fabricó un gol de barrio. Con la puntera, al contrapié del portero, cruzado. Delantero Pichichi. El desplome blanco fue llamativo. Tanto que brotaron silbidos. Tímidos al principio. Contundentes después de que Tsitiashvili se girase con comodidad y Courtois evitara el segundo. No acertaba a salir el Madrid, ni en conducción ni con balones largos, con Bernardo exhausto. Como si esperase a esa jugada directa de contra para rematar la faena en lugar de darse un gustazo. Claro, tenía que reaccionar Mourinho porque el asunto se le iba de las manos. Primero metió a Tchouaméni por un cansado Bernardo. Y después entró Arda Güler, que es otro rollo. Sustituyó a Diomande, que dejó trabajo y buenos detalles, no menos que otros de sus compañeros. El caso es que el turco dio la vuelta al partido como un calcetín. Porque la pide, se ofrece, la aguanta y la juega. Lo hizo todo bien. Pasó, tiró, se movió y acabó sirviendo el pase de la sentencia (tras una buena salida de Camavinga, todo hay que decirlo) a Mbappé, que alcanza en el Pichichi a Camello y Raphinha. Hay pelea. Donde no hay duda es con Güler. Arda y diez más.

articles.title: Dante Moore, No. 6 Oregon Upset by Oklahoma St., Box Score Stats, Draft Stock After Historic Loss
articles.summary: No. 6 Oregon suffered a shocking 39-31 upset loss at the hands of Oklahoma State on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
No. 6 Oregon suffered a shocking 39-31 upset loss at the hands of Oklahoma State on Saturday afternoon.

The Cowboys entered the contest on a 12-game losing streak, becoming the first team with a double-digit losing streak to ever defeat a top-10 opponent.

Ducks quarterback Dante Moore bounced back from a shaky first half, but it wasn't enough to help his team emerge victorious.

As Moore's inability to beat Oklahoma State may have hurt his draft stock, fans and pundits were surprised by the outcome of the overall game.

The Ducks didn't appear to be on the verge of an upset loss at the beginning of Saturday's matchup, holding a 7-3 lead at the end of the first quarter due to a 96-yard pick-six by linebacker Devon Jackson.

However, Oklahoma State's offense exploded in the second quarter as Oregon struggled to keep up.

The Cowboys finished with 21 points in the quarter compared to just 10 for the Ducks, gaining a 24-17 lead at halftime. Moore was just 5-of-15 for 45 yards in the first half.

Oklahoma State extended its advantage to 27-17 with a field goal on its opening drive of the third quarter, but Oregon quickly responded with a 36-yard touchdown pass by Moore.

An ensuing Cowboys field goal put them up by six points, but the Ducks finally jumped back in front with a 38-yard touchdown connection between Moore and Evan Stewart.

The shootout continued shortly afterwards, as Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker scrambled for a 10-yard rushing touchdown to give his squad a 36-31 lead on the next drive.

The Ducks' offense finally stalled down the stretch of the game, picking up just 11 total yards on their next three possessions combined. One drive ended in a punt, while the other two resulted in turnovers.

This included an unexpected decision by Oregon head coach Dan Lanning to attempt a fourth-down conversion with eight yards to gain at his own 33-yard line with just under seven minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. The Ducks were unable to move the chains, setting up an Oklahoma State field goal.

Lanning's team consistently failed to extend drives, converting just five of 14 opportunities on third down. Oregon also struggled on the ground, compiling a mere 90 rush yards on 30 attempts.

The Ducks are now 1-1, as their latest defeat should be a cause for concern moving forward.

articles.title: Oklahoma State shocks No. 6 Oregon 39-31 a year after Ducks blitzed the Cowboys by 66 points
articles.summary: Oregon beat Oklahoma State 69-3 a season ago.
articles.body:
A week after losing to Tulsa and a year after losing by more than 60 points to Oregon , the Cowboys shocked the No. 6 Ducks 39-31 on Saturday.

Oregon, a 24-point favorite, was somehow even sloppier than it was in its Week 1 win over Boise State . And the epitome of that adjective came just after the two-minute warning. As Oregon needed a touchdown and a 2-point conversion to tie the game, RB Dierre Hill Jr. simply dropped a toss from QB Dante Moore and Oklahoma State recovered.

Oregon had three timeouts after the fumble, but QB Drew Mestemaker kept the ball on a third-down read option to seal the game with a run for a first down.

"I don't know if I can top this," OSU coach Eric Morris told ESPN after the game. "I'm not going to retire but I might think about it tonight."

Mestemaker showed why he's a potential first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft in the win. He was 26-of-43 passing for 317 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing six times for 109 yards and a score. He broke a 75-yard run on the first play of the game and his leaping touchdown run in the fourth quarter put the Cowboys up for good.

Mestemaker transferred to Oklahoma State after the 2025 season when Morris left North Texas for Oklahoma State. Mestemaker, who famously didn't start for his high school team and was a walk-on for the Mean Green, threw for 4,379 yards and 34 touchdowns at North Texas in 2025.

His OSU career got off to a rough start, however. He was just 29-of-49 passing for 241 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in the Cowboys' loss to Tulsa to open the season. The 24-10 defeat was Oklahoma State's second straight loss to the Golden Hurricane. Last year's loss led to the firing of longtime coach Mike Gundy.

This year, Week 1 made it look like Morris had a mountain to climb in Stillwater and that Mestemaker, RB Caleb Hawkins , WR Wyatt Young and the other former North Texas players who followed him to OSU were in for a rough transition to the Big 12. Especially given the way that Oregon demolished the Cowboys in 2025.

Oregon beat Oklahoma State 69-3 a season ago as it rolled up 631 total yards and forced two Oklahoma State turnovers. That loss came less than a week before the defeat to Tulsa as OSU finished the season 1-11 and didn't beat a team at the top level of college football all season long.

Moore has been seen as the top quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft class after his decision to return for another season with the Ducks . After throwing for three touchdowns in Oregon's Week 1 win over Boise State, he got off to a rough start on Saturday. At one point, Moore was 3-of-11 passing for 17 yards as Oregon's receivers also didn't give him much help.

Moore finished the game 14-of-29 passing for 191 yards and two scores. Oregon mustered just 281 total yards of offense to Oklahoma State's 554, and the Cowboys had 25 first downs to Oregon's 12.

The stats don't simply tell the story of how poorly Oregon played, however. Before the fourth-quarter fumble, Oregon's previous two drives were inexcusable. After Mestemaker's TD, the Ducks somehow committed two delay-of-game penalties in four plays before punting the ball. The first came after the kickoff and before first down. The second came as the team lined up to punt.

After getting the ball back with 7:22 to go and trailing by five, Oregon gained just 2 yards on its first three plays of the drive. Rather than punting the ball back to Oklahoma State, Oregon coach Dan Lanning elected to go for it on fourth-and-8 from his own 33 yard-line. Moore's pass to Evan Stewart was nowhere close to being complete, and Oklahoma State tacked on a field goal after taking over possession for an eight-point lead.

Was the decision to go for it a clear sign that Lanning was concerned that his defense couldn't stop Oklahoma State? The Cowboys averaged over 6 yards a play on Saturday and the number was much higher until they slowed the game down in the fourth quarter. And two tipped passes were also a big reason why Oregon was even competitive in the first place.

The Ducks' first touchdown came on a 96-yard pick-6 by Devon Jackson in the first quarter, and a second interception off a deflected pass set up the Ducks at the 1-yard line for their second TD in the second quarter.

Had those passes not fallen into the arms of Oregon defenders, the game could have been a rout. It wasn't, but it's still Oregon's second embarrassing loss in its last three games after Indiana blew out the Ducks 56-22 in the semifinals of the College Football Playoff a season ago.

That loss helped prompt Moore and other key members of the team to return for a run at the national title in 2026. Through two weeks of the season, a national title looks like a long shot. Heck, Oregon doesn't even look like a playoff team.

articles.title: Mourinho: "Si hoy no juega Diomande de titular, la primera pregunta habría sido: '¿Por qué no juega Diomande?'"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador madridista analizó la victoria ante el Rayo en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: El entrenador madridista analizó la victoria ante el Rayo en el Bernabéu
articles.body: El Real Madrid regresó a la senda de la victoria en Liga. Los de Mourinho vencieron por 4-1 al Rayo en un partido que mostró las dos caras de los blancos. El técnico analizó la victoria en rueda de prensa. Güler: "Arda juega mucho cuando está en el campo. Voy a decir 100% seguro que si hoy no juega Diomande de titular, la primera pregunta hubiera sido '¿Por qué no juega Diomande?'. En el banquillo solo se ve calidad. Las permutas van a pasar partido a partido. Arda tiene una influencia muy positiva en el juego del equipo. Cuando entró, marcó las diferencias en la estabilidad del juego". Diferencias entre las dos mitades: "Definiría el partido como uno de 45'. En 45', acabado. Sabía que el equipo no tenía fuerza física y mental para jugar el segundo tiempo como ha jugado. La imagen que ilustra todo es cómo Bellingham ha jugado los últimos 10 minutos. Prácticamente todos ha cometido errores en construcción, la dificultad para presionar, los tiros a puerta... Ya lo sabía. Me esperaba que iba a ser así". ¿Hay algo que le preocupa de su equipo?: "Estoy contento porque estamos juntos desde hace tres meses, aunque solo podemos contar desde que estamos todos. Lo que estamos haciendo tiene muchas cosas positivas. Vamos poco a poco, intentando mejorar siempre". Diomande: "Estoy un poco mayor para sentir presión. Tienes diferentes plantillas, algunas veces tienes que rezar para que nadie se haga mal, otras donde tienes muchas soluciones. Va a ir progresivamente mejorando. Tiene poco tiempo en alto nivel y tiene mucho que aprender del punto de vista táctico. Pero tiene un potencial increíble. En el uno contra uno, pase, tiro... Nos da muchas opciones. Puede jugar donde Vini, en la derecha, Arda puede jugar allí o donde Bellingham. En este momento quiero hacerle evolucionar". Vinicius: "Físicamente está mejor que nunca. Le falta un milímetro para llegar a su velocidad máxima. La capacidad para repetir esfuerzos es enorme. Es un proceso que está asimilando. Mentalmente es muy fuerte, conoce al Madrid mejor que nadie. Juega con mucha responsabilidad, que es la de jugar para el Madrid y la selección brasileña. Está tranquilo. Llegarán los goles". Último cambio: "Fácil. Quiero ganar y quiero ganar con el máximo posible de goles. Cuando estás 3-1, con 5' por jugar, tienes a un lateral muy potente en el Rayo capaz de crear peligro... Ahí me ha parecido que es mejor cerrar la puerta. El tiempo de hacer filigranas y meter goles para mí había terminado. Después hicimos el cuarto, todavía mejor".

articles.title: Francia 'empaña' el debut de Audero
articles.standfirst: Dos errores de Lejeune y un par de goles de Mbappé provocaron tres de los cuatro tantos al debutante en la portería que evitó una mayor goleada en la segunda mitad
articles.summary: Dos errores de Lejeune y un par de goles de Mbappé provocaron tres de los cuatro tantos al debutante en la portería que evitó una mayor goleada en la segunda mitad
articles.body: No siempre se puede ser el mejor. Florian Lejeune, uno de los mejores defensas del campeonato y estandarte del Rayo Vallecano no tuvo su mejor primera parte en el Bernabéu. El central provocó el penalti que transformó su compatriota Mbappé y luego erró en una salida de balón que acabó con el gol de Carreras. Estos errores penalizaron a un Rayo Vallecano que luego recibiría el tercero en el minuto 35. Los tres tantos fueron encajados por Emil Audero, nuevo fichaje del Rayo Vallecano, que poco pudo hacer en ellos y se esperó para brillar en la segunda parte. El cuadro franjirrojo se sacudió en la segunda mitad. Salió como si el resultado fuera de empate a cero y consiguió meterse en el encuentro con un gol de Sergio Camello que ya lleva seis. Otro de los nombres propios fue el de Lejeune, que a pesar de errar, volvió a ser el central solvente de siempre. En el minuto 53' realizó su característico 'cañonazo' desde fuera del área que amenazó la portería de Courtois que provocó el enfado de José Mourinho en el banquillo. Tres minutos después, dejó 'tirado' con un recorte a Jude Belllingham que entró con todo para robar la posesión. En el minuto 77 comenzó el recital de Emil Audero. Desvió al larguero un cabezazo potente de Dumfries y luego sacó el remate de Rüdiger en el córner posterior. En el minuto 80 realizó un paradón a Arda Güler que no se lo podía creer y un minuto más tarde le sacó un pie a Mbappé que quería redondear el resultado. Lo estaba sacando todo y parecía que el Rayo Vallecano se iría dos por abajo del Bernabéu. Sin embargo, el delantero francés no se había rendido y después de una arrancada de Camavinga y un pase de Güler, la puso al segundo palo con un disparo que rebotó en la madera antes de entrar. Audero tuvo un debut inolvidable en el Bernabéu con un resultado que no cuadró con su actuación.

articles.title: Sunderland 0-2 Arsenal: Bruno Guimaraes haunts Black Cats with stunner after David Raya penalty save
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes haunts Sunderland with a stunning goal as Arsenal win 2-0 at the Stadium of Light; David Raya saved an Enzo Le Fee penalty; Bukayo Saka added a late second from the spot
articles.body:
The Black Cats had the chance to go in front when Ezri Konsa was penalised for holding Dan Ballard in the second half, a decision which enraged Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, but Raya brilliantly tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot kick onto the post.

Just 121 seconds later, Guimaraes, whose every touch had been booed by the home fans due to his Newcastle connections, crashed a stunning strike in off the underside of the crossbar from outside the Sunderland box for his first Arsenal goal.

Arsenal had to withstand late pressure from the home side, with Raya saving well from Nordi Mukiele, but they made the result safe when Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty after Reinildo Mandava was shown a second yellow card for hauling him down.

The victory, Arsenal's fourth in a row in the Premier League and sixth in all competitions, maintains their strong start to the campaign and puts the champions three points above Manchester City, who face Manchester United live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

For Sunderland, the defeat is made all the more painful by the identity of the player who opened the scoring, coming so soon after they appeared poised to strike first from the spot. They remain on four points, the latest side to be dispatched by Mikel Arteta's men.

31: OVER! Odegaard cuts the ball back to Havertz after intricate build-up but the Arsenal forward blazes over

33: SAVE! Roefs tips an acrobatic effort from Havertz over the bar as Sunderland continue to hold firm

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports: "It's a huge win but it could have been something very different.

"I'm so upset. It's unacceptable (Sunderland's award of a penalty). This can change the course of a season, the championship, and it's not acceptable.

"I've seen it 10 times to make sure because I watched it live and I said it's not possible that it's going to be a penalty because it's a judo role, that's what it is. It cannot happen.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any context, in any league."

Guimaraes didn't hesitate when asked after the game if he sees David Raya as the best goalkeeper in the world. "Definitely," he said.

The midfielder's sensational goal completed the two-minute turnaround but it was Raya who made it possible.

Arteta was adamant the spot kick should never have been awarded. But Raya's sole focus was to stop it from going in. Le Fee, who scored a penalty last weekend, struck it well. Raya, though, showed his athleticism, diving low to his left to make the save.

It was a brilliant piece of goalkeeping and there were plenty of other examples over the course of the 90 minutes at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are about as physical as opponents come but he dominated his box, claiming crosses and exuding calm.

His save to deny Mukiele, following a fabulous centre by Granit Xhaka, when Arsenal were still only a goal up, was another crucial intervention. And he was straight back up on his feet to scramble away the follow-up. Raya is always alert to danger.

He had to settle for a place on the bench with Spain at the World Cup. But there can be little doubting his status as the Premier League's best, if not the world's, and his value to his team-mates and manager is abundantly clear.

He was Arsenal's difference-maker - and not for the first time.

Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes to TNT Sports: "It's unbelievable. I feel very good.

"Everyone knows I had a difficult start with injuries in a short time but I'm glad to be back, to play.

"I scored a beautiful goal. It's a beautiful moment for me and my family and I'm very happy.

"A beautiful goal in a very good place. Everyone knows my past. I had an amazing history at Newcastle but now I'm trying to create a new history here and I've started in the right way."

articles.title: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta rages at 'unacceptable' penalty against Sunderland
articles.summary: A furious Mikel Arteta hit out at a penalty given against Arsenal in the Premier League champion's 2-0 win against Sunderland on Saturday, saying such decisi...
articles.body:
SUNDERLAND, England (AP) — A furious Mikel Arteta hit out at a penalty given against Arsenal in the Premier League champion's 2-0 win against Sunderland on Saturday, saying such decisions could change the course of the season.

Sunderland was awarded a spot kick in the second half at the Stadium of Light when Arsenal's Ezri Konsa brought down Dan Ballard in the box.

The score was 0-0 at the time and Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya pushed away Enzo Le Fee 's penalty.

Despite Arsenal going on to win, Arteta was still seething about the decision.

"It's unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This changes the course of the season, the championship, and it's not acceptable," Arteta told TNT Sports.

Referees have been instructed to clamp down on infringements in the box during set-piece plays. The Premier League confirmed the penalty was given for a holding offense by Konsa on Ballard.

"I've seen it 10 times to make sure because I watched it live and I said it's not possible at this level that there's going to be a penalty," Arteta said. "I've been in football for almost 27 years, 28 years. It's not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league."

Bruno Guimaraes put Arsenal ahead two minutes after Raya saved from Le Fee. Bukayo Saka sealed the win with a penalty for Arsenal in added time.

articles.title: Blaze Berlowitz booed after fumble, blocked punt give Delaware lead vs Vanderbilt football
articles.summary: Quarterback Blaze Berlowitz was booed after committing a fumble against Delaware and the Blue Hens later took the lead on a blocked punt.
articles.body:
Vanderbilt football seemed to have control of its Sept. 12 contest against Delaware , leading by 11 late in the second quarter, but things quickly turned.

After several drives led by 5-star freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, including two touchdown drives, the Commodores opted to take a successful field goal off the board and attempt a 4th-and-2. Curtis' pass was complete but short of the sticks, and Delaware (1-0) scored a touchdown on the subsequent drive.

After that touchdown, Vanderbilt (1-0) switched quarterbacks, going back to Blaze Berlowitz , who had run the first two drives of the game. Berlowitz drove the Commodores to midfield, but he attempted to hurdle a defender on a run play and fumbled, recovered by the Blue Hens.

Inside Vanderbilt football vs Delaware: See our best photos from Game 2

Vanderbilt got the ball back after forcing a Delaware punt, but the Commodores stuck with Berlowitz on the next drive and he threw two incomplete passes then rushed for one yard, going three-and-out. Boos rang out for the first time from the crowd at FirstBank Stadium.

Things went from bad to worse when Tyler Ebel's punt was blocked and recovered by the Blue Hens for a touchdown with 17 seconds to go until half. Cheers of "Let's go Hens" rang out from a sizeable portion of Delaware fans in the stands.

Boos continued when Berlowitz came out to take a knee on the final play before half.

The Blue Hens took a 17-14 lead into halftime.
